## F-189 — Closing a DM stopped being a LIVE event: the tombstone-hiding RLS policy makes its own CDC frame undeliverable (2026-08-10)

- Location: `supabase/migrations/20260810100000_channels_rls_hide_tombstoned.sql:202-213` (`channels_member_select`, the `AND deleted_at IS NULL` conjunct); `src/features/channels/server/repository.ts#softDeleteChannel` (the UPDATE that becomes invisible); `service-writes.deleteChannel` (the DM branch) and `service-workspace-departure.ts` (the departure branch) are the two callers
- Found during: post-apply reasoning about what C-15's policy change costs, in the same wave that applied it
- Severity: **bug (liveness regression, accepted for now)** — no data loss, no security consequence; the room is still correctly hidden, just not *promptly*
- Status: **open, ACCEPTED.** Shipped knowingly in `1d11a31`; recorded here so the trade is not rediscovered as a mystery.

**THE MECHANISM, WHICH IS THE WHOLE FINDING.** `channels` is in the `supabase_realtime` publication (verified: `channel_consent_requests`, `channel_members`, `channel_messages`, `channels`). Closing a DM is an **UPDATE** that stamps `deleted_at` — and `realtime.apply_rls` evaluates the **NEW** record against the subscriber's SELECT policy before delivering. That policy now requires `deleted_at IS NULL`. So the row the frame is announcing is, by the same statement that produced the frame, no longer visible to the subscriber, **and the frame is dropped.** The close was previously deliverable for exactly the reason §7 records about soft deletes generally: an `UPDATE` produces a full new record carrying `workspace_id`, so the `workspace_id=eq.<id>` filter matched and the doorbell rang. C-15 did not break the filter; it made the row fail the policy the filter is checked alongside.

**EFFECT:** the peer's sidebar keeps rendering a DM that is closed until their next refetch. Nothing is wrong on screen except the timing — `listChannels` filters `deleted_at IS NULL`, so the next read drops it correctly. **This is a downgrade from live to next-refetch, not a stale-forever bug.**

**⚠ THE OBVIOUS GENERALIZATION IS THE TRAP: this is a property of EVERY soft-delete-hiding SELECT policy, not of DMs.** Any table where (a) the tombstone is an UPDATE, (b) the table is in the publication, and (c) the SELECT policy excludes tombstones, has silently traded its delete doorbell for a refetch. `channels` is the only one in this codebase today because it is the only table that still soft-deletes AND is published — but the next `deleted_at IS NULL` added to a published table's policy inherits this for free and will not be noticed, because the failure is a frame that does not arrive.

**REMEDY SKETCHED, NOT TAKEN — and the ORDER is the whole design.** Touch the peer's `channel_members` row (a no-op `UPDATE`, e.g. re-stamping a column it already carries) **BEFORE** stamping the channel tombstone. `channel_members` is published and carries `workspace_id` in its replica identity (`20260807150000`, `REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX`), so that UPDATE rides the existing `CHANNEL_TABLES` / `SYNC_TABLES` doorbell both subscribers already refetch on. It **must** come first: `channel_members_member_select` was rewritten in the same migration to require `c.deleted_at IS NULL` on the parent channel, so the identical touch performed AFTER the tombstone is dropped for exactly the reason this finding opens with. A remedy for this bug is one statement away from being another instance of it.

**NOTE THE ASYMMETRY BETWEEN THE TWO CALLERS, because it is why this reads as "sometimes live".** The ordinary DM close (`deleteChannel`) writes only the `channels` UPDATE and is therefore fully dark. The **workspace-departure** close (`service-workspace-departure.ts`) also DELETEs the leaver's `channel_members` row, and a DELETE's deliverability turns on the subscription filter against `old_columns` (= the replica identity, which carries `workspace_id`) with `old_record` PK-redacted, rather than on a policy evaluation — so that path probably still rings the doorbell. **Reasoned from the deployed identity and §7's `apply_rls` note, NOT observed** — treat it as a hypothesis, and if you ever need it to be true, verify it against a live frame first. Same class of owed verification as F-190.

## F-190 — `channel_members` CDC may have gone dark for `authenticated`, and we will not know until someone watches a frame (2026-08-10)

- Location: `supabase/migrations/20260810120000_channel_members_column_privileges.sql` (the `REVOKE SELECT ON public.channel_members FROM anon, authenticated` + per-column `GRANT`); rollback named in that file's header (`GRANT SELECT ON public.channel_members TO anon, authenticated;` — one statement)
- Found during: writing the migration; recorded as an accepted risk at apply time, not discovered afterwards
- Severity: **bug (potential outage, unobserved)** — the security property holds either way; what is at risk is a doorbell
- Status: **open — VERIFICATION OWED AT FIRST LIVE OBSERVATION.** Do not close this by reasoning; close it by watching a roster change propagate.

**WHAT C-15 DID AND WHY IT IS A COLUMN PRIVILEGE.** Samuel's ruling: per-member settings are private, role and roster basics stay public. `dto.mapMemberRow` already scrubbed `agent_tool_profile` — but the DTO **is not on every path**, which is the sentence the old docblock got wrong. `channel_members` is published and `authenticated` held table-wide SELECT, so the RAW row reached any channel member over CDC and over PostgREST with the anon key the browser ships. **A column privilege binds both consumers where a policy binds neither** (RLS filters rows, not columns), which is why the enforcement moved to `REVOKE` + a per-column `GRANT` rather than to another policy.

**THE FAILURE MODE, STATED AS A CONDITIONAL BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT IT IS.** `realtime.apply_rls` redacts per column — but **if the deployed build tests table-level SELECT before it reaches the column loop**, the `REVOKE` reads as "no SELECT at all" and **every `channel_members` frame goes dark for `authenticated`**, not just the redacted column. That is not a security regression (dark is the safe direction) — it is the loss of the roster doorbell that §7 records as *already paid for* and that F-189's remedy proposes to lean on. Two findings would then be resting on a frame that no longer arrives.

**WHY IT WAS SHIPPED ANYWAY.** The security property is the ruling and it holds under either behaviour; the failure is degraded liveness with a **one-statement rollback** already written into the migration header. Shipping and watching costs less than staging a realtime harness for a question one live roster change answers.

**⚠ WHAT "VERIFY" MEANS HERE, precisely — because the wrong verification will read as a pass.** Do NOT verify by querying `information_schema.column_privileges`; that confirms the grant landed, which is not in doubt. Verify by **subscribing as an `authenticated` client and making a roster change** (add or remove a member), then checking whether the frame arrives and whether `agent_tool_profile` is absent from it. Three outcomes: frame arrives without the column (intended — close this finding); frame arrives WITH the column (the redaction does not bind CDC at all — a real leak, roll back and rethink); no frame (this finding is confirmed — roll back and find another shape). **And do not verify against upstream `walrus` master**, for the same reason §7 already warns about `apply_rls`: its master returns `coalesce(..., true)` in the neighbouring branch and says the opposite of what is deployed.

**THE STANDING RULE THIS LEAVES BEHIND (also in ENGINEERING §7/§8):** a new per-member SETTING must be added to `dto.mapMemberRow`'s scrub **AND** left out of that migration's `GRANT` list. Two edits, and the second is the one that binds. Adding it to only the scrub reproduces exactly the gap C-15 closed.

## F-191 — The C-20 sweep removes the member but not their SESSION and THREAD-PARTICIPANT rows (2026-08-10)

- Location: `src/features/channels/server/service-workspace-departure.ts#removeWorkspaceDepartedMember` (touches `channel_members` and `channels.deleted_at`, and nothing else); the unswept tables are `public.channel_sessions` (`20260805120000`) and `public.channel_task_participants` (`20260731130000`)
- Found during: verifying C-20's sweep half against the tables that carry a `user_id` alongside a channel
- Severity: smell (correctness of derived reads, no security consequence) — promoted from "not noticed" to "written down" precisely because the sweep's own docblock enumerates what it deliberately skips and these two are not in that list
- Status: open
- **Measured 2026-08-10 (production): 0 orphaned `channel_task_participants`, 0 orphaned `channel_sessions`, 0 ghost `channel_members`.** So this is a LATENT code gap, not an observed data problem — which is the honest framing and also the reason it is a smell rather than a bug. The C-20 backfill migration (`20260810140000`) found zero ghosts for the same reason: nobody has left this workspace yet.

**WHY IT MATTERS EVEN AT ZERO ROWS.** C-20's whole thesis is that a departed member must be *removed*, not *filtered* — Samuel's words were "fully and cleanly removed". The sweep delivers that for the roster, which is the table with a BEHAVIOUR attached (`classify`'s implicit trigger keys on an exact `memberCount === 2`). These two tables have no such trigger, so the cost is smaller: a departed user's rows keep appearing in session lists and thread participant sets, i.e. the same "roster keeps rendering someone who left" the sweep exists to end, one layer down. **The gap is not that the rows are dangerous; it is that "fully removed" is now true of one table and false of two, and nothing says so.**

**`channel_trust` WAS FINE AND WAS NEVER PART OF THIS — verified, not assumed.** `trust-service.ts` called `repo.isActiveWorkspaceMember(ctx.workspaceId, …)` on both the read and the grant path, so a trust rule naming a departed user was inert the moment they left. That is the shape this finding is asking for on the other two, and it is worth noting that trust got there by **re-checking at read** rather than by sweeping at write — which is cheaper, needs no departure hook, and is the design to consider first. ⚠ **THE TABLE AND THE FILE ARE BOTH DELETED (2026-08-22, INVARIANTS §6)** — `agent_trust_rules` is dropped with the inbound consent lane, so it is no longer one of the tables a departure sweep would have to consider at all. The lesson survives the code; the reference does not.

**Proposed resolution — read the sweep's docblock before choosing.** Either (a) extend `removeWorkspaceDepartedMember` with two more deletes, or (b) filter at read the way trust does. **(b) is likely right for `channel_sessions`** (a session is an ephemeral fact and a departed user's is definitionally over) and **(a) for `channel_task_participants`** (a participant set is durable and is read for addressing). Whichever is chosen, the choice belongs in that docblock's "WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SWEEP" section, which currently names only `channel_tasks`.

## F-192 — The desktop DMG downloads at ~0.9 MB/s: the landing page serves 195 MB straight off GitHub release assets, with no CDN (2026-08-10)

- Location: the landing-page download link → GitHub release asset URL (no intermediary); no Cloudflare/R2 or any other CDN in front of it
- Found during: a real download, timed
- Severity: smell (product/conversion, not correctness) — recorded because it is the first thing a new user experiences and nothing in the tree measures it
- Status: open — **needs Samuel's Cloudflare account, so it is gated on him, not on code**

**MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED:** ~**0.9 MB/s** sustained, for a **195 MB** artifact ≈ **4 minutes** of staring at a progress bar before the app has done anything. GitHub release assets are not a CDN for this purpose: they are unaccelerated for most geographies and the rate is not something the repo can tune.

**WHY THIS IS WORTH AN ID rather than a TODO.** Every other launch-readiness item in this tree is about what happens *after* someone is running the app. This one is entirely *before*, it is on the only path a new user takes, and four minutes is comfortably past where downloads get abandoned. It is also the cheapest item on the list to fix relative to its reach.

**FIX SKETCHED:** put R2 (or any CDN) in front of the download and point the landing page at it, with the release asset as the origin so the publish flow does not change. **The blocker is an account, not an implementation** — this needs Samuel's Cloudflare account before anyone writes anything, so do not open a branch for it first. Two things to decide when it is unblocked: whether the auto-updater's feed moves too (it pulls from the same release assets and has the same problem, less visibly, on every update for every existing user), and whether the artifact itself can shrink — 195 MB is an Electron bundle and part of that number is a packaging question, not a delivery one.

## F-196 — Any Stripe plan change mints a FRESH credit period key, and the counter starts over (2026-08-11)

- Location: `src/features/billing/credits.ts › resolveCreditPeriod` (the anchor branch) fed by `src/features/billing/server/webhook-handler.ts › subscriptionFields` → `currentPeriodStart`; the counter is keyed `(workspace_id, period_start)` in `workspace_credit_usage` (`supabase/migrations/20260811130000_mcp_credits.sql`)
- Found during: the adversarial review of the credits system, filed while fixing B1–B3
- Severity: smell — an abuse path with a real cost attached to it, not a free one
- Description: `period_start` IS the partition key of the credit counter, and Stripe re-anchors `current_period_start` on any subscription change (upgrade, downgrade, price swap, and the first `subscription.updated` a workspace sees after a deploy). A new anchor is a new key, and a new key has `used = 0` — so a plan change hands out a **full fresh allowance mid-month**, and solo↔team cycling hands out an unbounded number of them. The bound is Stripe's proration arithmetic, not anything in this tree: each cycle costs the operator real money, which is why this is a smell and not a blocker.
- Note it is NOT the cancellation bug (B2, fixed 2026-08-11): that one was a STALE anchor keeping an old counter alive. This is the mirror image — a NEW anchor abandoning a live one. The free-verdict rule that fixes B2 does nothing here, because both sides of the swap are paid verdicts.
- Proposed resolution — two sketches, neither implemented: (a) carry `used` FORWARD when re-anchoring inside the same calendar month (an upsert that seeds the new key from the old one, so the swap is not a reset); or (b) key the counter on the **truncated month of the anchor** rather than the anchor instant, which makes the key stable across re-anchoring by construction and costs one `date_trunc`. (b) is the smaller change and loses the exact billing-date boundary; (a) preserves it and needs a migration-time decision about what "the old one" means when several exist.
- Status: open

## F-197 — The credit consume route is viewer-callable and write-scope exempt: any member token can drain the workspace allowance (2026-08-11)

- Location: `src/app/api/mcp/credits/consume/route.ts` (`withWorkspaceAuth(…, { writeScopeExempt: true })`, `minRole` defaulted to `viewer`)
- Found during: the same adversarial review
- Severity: smell — gated on a product decision, not on code
- Description: the route spends one credit per call and both of its gate relaxations are deliberate and documented (every MCP caller is an OAuth agent token, so `sessionOnly` would refuse the only legitimate caller; a READ-ONLY session still consumes, because the cost is the tool call, not the write). The consequence is that **any active member — viewer included — holding any token can POST the route in a loop and burn the workspace's monthly allowance without making a single tool call.** The net effect is the same as looping real MCP calls, which is also uncapped, so this does not open a hole the tool surface did not already have; it just makes it one hop cheaper. `checkAndRecordRateLimitSubject` bounds the speed at 600/min.
- Why it is not fixed here: the obvious lever — raise `minRole` — **breaks legitimate viewer agents**, which are a supported shape (a read-only agent token is exactly the case `writeScopeExempt` exists for). Any real fix is a product call about who is allowed to spend a workspace's credits, not a wrapper option.
- Proposed resolution: defer to Samuel. If it needs a code answer before that, a per-actor sub-budget (spend attributed to `userId`, capped as a fraction of the workspace allowance) is the shape that does not break viewer agents.
- Status: open — needs a product decision

## F-198 — Metering is enforced on the hosted MCP transport only; a bearer token calling REST routes directly is uncharged (2026-08-11)

- Location: the charge lives at `packages/mcp-server/src/registrar.ts › createCreditedRunner` (the per-tool-call wrapper), which is on the `/api/mcp` transport path; every `src/app/api/**` route reached with the same OAuth token runs `withWorkspaceAuth` and is NOT charged
- Found during: the same adversarial review
- Severity: statement of scope, not a bug — recorded so nobody reads "MCP calls are metered" as "agent traffic is metered"
- Description: the registrar is the only exactly-once-per-tool-call seam there is (one tool call makes 0..N loopback requests), which is why the charge sits there and explicitly not in `withWorkspaceAuth`. The cost of that correct choice is that the REST surface underneath — the same routes the loopback client calls, reachable with the same agent token — is free. An agent author who skips the MCP server and drives the REST API gets the product uncharged.
- This is a DELIBERATE boundary and it is not obviously wrong: the REST API is the product's own API, the credit is a price on the MCP convenience layer, and moving the charge down would double-count every tool call by its loopback fan-out. **Written down because the alternative is someone later reading the meter as a global usage cap and building on that.**
- Proposed resolution: none proposed. If the boundary ever needs to move, the unit has to change first — a per-REQUEST price, not a per-TOOL-CALL one — and that is a pricing decision, not a refactor.
- Status: open (accepted residual)

## F-199 — The bundled SPA is NOT realtime-dark, and three surviving comments said it was (2026-08-18) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-30

- Location of the false claim: `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/channels/index.tsx › ChannelsPage` ("⚠ REALTIME IS OFF HERE … `shared-channel-registry.ts` short-circuits on `window.dopl`"), `apps/desktop-ui/src/components/app-shell/app-shell.tsx › AppShellLayout` ("POLLED because realtime is a no-op in the SPA"), `dopl-desktop-app/main/ui-sync.js`'s own header ("short-circuits to a no-op the moment it sees the SPA bridge"), and inherited by `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/channels-v2/MAPPING.md` § *Not represented in the mock*

With `onSyncEvent` + `syncWatch` present it returns `› subscribeViaBridge`; only their ABSENCE (an older main) returns the no-op

- What was verified, 2026-08-18: `dopl-desktop-app/renderer/app-preload.js` exposes both `syncWatch` and `onSyncEvent`, and `dopl-desktop-app/test/preload-parity.test.mjs › APP_OPS` pins them by name. - **Commit archaeology (hashes verified with `git show -s`, 2026-08-18).** The docblock landed in `1f614c1a` at 00:29:43 -0700 on 2026-08-03 and was TRUE when written. `90201de5` at 00:55:42 — **26 minutes later** — gave the registry its bridge branch and the preload its two sync ops. `channel_messages` / `agent_presence` were still excluded from the feed at that point (they sat in `LISTENER_OWNED_TABLES` under the channels exemption), so the transcript really did stay dark for another two and a half hours; `c4ba401d` at 03:07:37 moved all three into `SYNC_TABLES` — *"First channels dogfood froze the transcript … the exemption's object is the listener MODULES, not the UI's right to live messages"* — and emptied `LISTENER_OWNED_TABLES`. `1beaaf40` (14:52) dropped the file's `NOT WIRED YET` marker. **Nobody went back to the page docblock in any of those four commits.**
- `docs/INVARIANTS.md` §7 was never wrong about this — it describes the feed correctly and always has. The failure is that the SPA page comments were the nearest thing to hand and they were louder
- Fixed in this change: both `apps/desktop-ui` docblocks, the `ui-sync.js` header clause, and the MAPPING.md parenthetical. §7 gained an explicit sentence so the next reader does not have to re-derive it from `SYNC_TABLES`
- Pinned so it cannot silently regress: `src/shared/realtime/shared-channel-registry.test.ts` now drives the real channels table constants through the bridge branch, and `dopl-desktop-app/test/ui-sync-tables.test.mjs` names all five channel tables individually with the transcript-freeze reason
- Status: open only as a LESSON — the claim is corrected everywhere it was found. **A comment is a measurement with no date on it. This one was falsified 26 minutes after it was written and survived fifteen days of work on the files around it.**
- ⚠ **CLOSED 2026-08-30 — superseded:** all three false comments are corrected in the tree. `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/channels/index.tsx › ChannelsPage` now reads *"REALTIME IS LIVE HERE"* and cites F-199/F-200, `ui-sync.js`'s header states that the UI feed watches the channel tables, and the capability-keyed branch is pinned at `src/shared/realtime/shared-channel-registry.ts › subscribeSharedWorkspaceTables`. INVARIANTS §7 remains the statement of record.

## F-203 — Tracked `packages/*/dist` is stale against `src`, and a plain rebuild proves it (2026-08-18) — ⚠ RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-30 — still open

- Measured 2026-08-18: with a clean tree, `npm run build:packages` rewrote **152 tracked files** under `packages/dopl-client/dist` and `packages/mcp-server/dist` (+3659 / −6136), the overwhelming majority of them unrelated to anything being changed — e.g. `packages/dopl-client/dist/abort.js`'s header still carried a docblock revision its `src` no longer has. Re-run the command on a clean tree to re-measure; do not quote the number
- So the committed `dist` is the output of some OLDER `src`, and `docs/INVARIANTS.md` §10's *"`packages/*/dist` is what the app loads at runtime — after editing either package's `src/`, run `npm run build:packages` or the old surface ships"* has silently not been happening
- Severity: depends entirely on a question this finding does not answer — **whether any consumer loads the committed `dist` rather than a rebuilt one.** `npm run build` (the deploy build) runs `build:packages` first, so the WEB deploy is unaffected. The desktop bundle and any local `node` entry point that imports `packages/mcp-server/dist` directly are the paths that would ship the stale surface. **Establish which, before deciding.**
- Deliberately NOT resolved in Phase 1: the rebuild was reverted rather than committed, because 152 files of unrelated regenerated output inside a read-model change buries the change and asserts, on someone else's behalf, that the whole regenerated surface is intended
- Proposed resolution, once the consumer question is answered: either (a) `dist` is a build artifact for every consumer → gitignore it and delete it from the index, or (b) some consumer really loads it → commit a deliberate full rebuild ON ITS OWN, and add the rebuild to a gate so it cannot drift again. **What is not acceptable is the current state, where the tree says one thing and the build says another**
- Status: open (needs a decision, not a patch)
- ⚠ **NOT SUPERSEDED — STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-30.** Neither branch of the decision this entry demands has been taken: `dist` is still tracked (218 files), `.gitignore` carries no `dist` entry, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` BUILDS both packages as a precondition but **never diffs the rebuild against the committed tree** — so there is still no gate.
- 🔴 **AND THE DRIFT IS LIVE, MEASURED BY DOING WHAT THIS ENTRY ASKS FOR (2026-08-30).** A plain `npm run build -w @dopl/mcp-server` rewrote **three modules that nothing in that change had touched** — `dist/tools/agent-shared.{js,d.ts}`, `dist/tools/knowledge-ops-write.{js,d.ts}` and `dist/tools/knowledge.js` — and one of them was not a comment: the committed `opUpdateBase` still had the FIVE-argument signature with no `shelf` refusal, so **the shelf-is-fixed-at-create ruling (F-342) was in `src/` and not in the build the MCP server loads.** The one example this entry cited (`dist/abort.js`'s header) HAS healed; the class has not.
- **The consumer question this entry says to answer first now has an answer for at least one path:** `scripts/check-role-drift.ts` reads the committed `dist/` deliberately, *"because it is what `main` actually imports"*. So option (a) — gitignore it — is not free; it would blind that gate. **Option (b) — a deliberate full rebuild plus a CI rebuild-diff step — is the branch the evidence now points at.**
- Status: **open (needs a decision, not a patch) — with the 2026-08-30 measurement above as the evidence it was waiting for.**

## F-204 — `react-hooks/refs` catches the assign-a-ref-during-render pattern in one channels file and not in its twin (2026-08-18)

- Two files wrote a ref in the render pass, the same way, for the same reason (a realtime callback needs the LATEST refetch closure without resubscribing): the retired two-pane page's `ChannelsViewCore` (`refetchRef.current = () => {…}`, `membersRefetchRef.current = …`) and `src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/channels-v2-core.tsx › ChannelsV2Core`. ⚠ **THE FIRST FILE NO LONGER EXISTS** — it was deleted at the v2 cutover (wiring plan Phase 12, 2026-08-18), so its anchor is history and the ORIGINAL measurement below cannot be re-run
- **Measured 2026-08-18, before the deletion:** `npx eslint src/features/channels/components/channels-view-core.tsx` → exit 0, zero diagnostics. The identical lines in the v2 core → **two `react-hooks/refs` errors**
- The v2 core was fixed at the time, and the older file was deliberately left alone as the then-shipping page. ⚠ **RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-18 (fix wave 3): "the refs are assigned in a `useEffect`" is no longer true OF THE V2 CORE — `channels-v2-core.tsx` holds no `refetchRef` at all.** The shape MOVED into the layer: `shared/hooks/use-api-mutation.ts › useRefetchGate` keeps its own `runRef` and assigns it in a `useEffect`, and the core just registers with the gate. So the fix outlived the file it was made in, which is the good outcome — but a reader chasing "the assignment in the v2 core" will find nothing and conclude the finding is stale. **The disagreement is now gone BY DELETION, not by diagnosis** — which resolves the symptom and leaves the cause exactly where it was
- What is NOT established: WHY the rule is silent on the older file. The plausible cause is a React-compiler bailout on that component (it declares several `async function` handlers inside the body, and the compiler-backed rules emit nothing for a component they decline to compile) — **that is a hypothesis, not a measurement.** Establish it before acting on it
- Why it matters beyond one file: a lint whose coverage silently varies per file trains readers to conclude "the older file does it, so it is fine". It is not fine in either file — a ref read by a subscription callback that fires before the render commits is the exact failure the rule names
- Proposed resolution: confirm the bailout, then either move `channels-view-core.tsx`'s two assignments into an effect the same way (small, mechanical, its own change) or record the bailout in `eslint.config.mjs` so the gap is visible. Whichever, the two files should not disagree
- ⚠ **SECOND INSTANCE, AND THE HYPOTHESIS IS NOW BETTER SUPPORTED (2026-08-18, Phase 8).** A different compiler-backed rule, `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, behaves the same way on the feature-detect-after-mount idiom. `src/features/channels/components/session-card.tsx` (`setBridge(getDesktopSessions())` inside a mount effect) and `src/features/channels/hooks/use-channel-folder.ts` / `use-channel-permission-preset.ts` (the same shape) all lint **clean**; a throwaway probe component containing byte-equivalent code, in the same directory, errored **immediately**. So the rule is not silent on the PATTERN — it is silent on those FILES, which is what a per-component bailout looks like. Still short of proof: nobody has read the compiler's bailout output
  - ⚠ **`session-card.tsx` IS DELETED (wiring plan Phase 5, 2026-08-18) — that half of the measurement is now UNREPEATABLE, exactly like the `channels-view-core.tsx` half above.** What survives and is still re-runnable is the pair that matters: `hooks/use-channel-folder.ts` and `hooks/use-channel-permission-preset.ts` are in the shipping tree, carry the same shape, and still lint clean. **Re-run against those two, not against the deleted card.** Two of this entry's three original exhibits have now been resolved by DELETION rather than by diagnosis, which is the reason to write the cause down before the last one goes
- Consequence, recorded so it is not mistaken for a style preference: `components/launch-panel.tsx` reads the same "is the desktop bridge here" fact with `useSyncExternalStore` (never-notifying subscribe, a `getServerSnapshot` of `false`) instead of `useState` + a mount effect, because the effect form does not lint in a component the compiler accepts. **The tree now has two idioms for one question**, and which one a file gets is decided by whether the linter can compile it — a bad reason. Whoever resolves this finding should pick one and say so
  - ⚠ **THE `useSyncExternalStore` IDIOM HAS SPREAD: TWO CALLERS as of 2026-08-18** (`grep -rn useSyncExternalStore src/`) — `components/launch-panel.tsx` and `components/channels-v2/pop-out.tsx`, which took it for the same reason and says so in its own docblock. **That is the finding getting worse, not better:** an idiom picked to route around a linter bailout is now the pattern a new file copies, and nothing records that it was a workaround rather than a preference. Re-count before quoting; the number is what makes "two idioms" a trend instead of an exception
- Status: open (v2 half fixed; the older file went with the cutover rather than being understood — **the SECOND-rule instance and the CAUSE are still open**, and they are the half worth keeping: `set-state-in-effect` is silent on `use-channel-folder.ts` / `use-channel-permission-preset.ts` today, in the shipping tree, and the two-idioms consequence below is live)

## F-205 — The v2 Tags inbox's scroll target points at message ids that do not exist (2026-08-18)

- Location: `src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/fixtures-mentions.ts` (the rows) → `› channel-surface.tsx › openMention` → `› message-pane.tsx`'s scroll effect, which looks the row up by `[data-message-id]`. ⚠ **Anchor repointed 2026-08-23, historical location only:** `openMention` lived in `› channels-v2-core.tsx` when this was written and moved out with the channel-surface extraction. Nothing about the finding changed.
- The transcript's scroll plumbing is REAL and exercised (`transcript.test.tsx` pins `data-message-id`); the mentions inbox that drives it is fixture-driven until wiring-plan Phase 6, and its `messageId` values name no stored message. **So a click marks read, sets the thread and fires a nonced target that resolves to nothing.** Nothing throws — the effect returns early on a miss
- Deliberate, and the alternative was worse: pointing fixture rows at whatever real messages happen to be loaded would make the inbox assert that a real person tagged the viewer, which is a fabricated claim about somebody's words. The heatmap claims nothing about anybody; a mention does
- Phase 6 replaces the fixture with mention-addressed rows plus a read-state store (`channel_messages` has no read-state column today), at which point the ids are real and this closes without a code change to the plumbing
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-18 (Phase 6), and exactly as predicted — the plumbing was not touched.** `fixtures-mentions.ts` is deleted; the rows are the real projection (`server/service-mentions.ts › listMyChannelMentions`), so `messageId` now names a stored `channel_messages` row and the nonced target resolves. `message-pane.tsx`'s scroll effect, its nonce and the `[data-message-id]` lookup are byte-for-byte unchanged
- Status: RESOLVED

## F-206 — A requester cannot see whether their addressee approved, so the fan-out card cannot state per-target consent (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 3 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md` (the New-agent-thread panel + the request fan-out), building the posted request card
- **The shape.** A "New agent thread" send raises N threads, one per addressee, rendered as ONE card with one pill per person (`src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/transcript.tsx › ThreadCardMessage`). The mock the card is ported from puts a per-pill APPROVAL state on it — "1 of 3 agents approved". **There is no read that can answer that question for the requester.**
- **Why, and it is a design property rather than an oversight.** Consent is a per-target server-side ROW, and every read of it is scoped to `(operator, workspace)` with the operator ALWAYS `ctx.userId` — never from the body (`docs/INVARIANTS.md` §6; `src/features/channels/server/consent-service.ts › listConsentRequests`, `› requireOperatorRow`). The row is the ADDRESSEE's, so only the addressee's own client can read it. `requireOperatorRow` deliberately collapses missing / foreign-operator / cross-workspace into ONE 404 so ids cannot be probed
- **What was built instead, and why it is not the same thing.** `src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/view-model-requested.ts › requestedThreadIds` derives the MIRROR IMAGE from the viewer's own consent inbox — "threads YOU were asked about and have not answered" — by joining the pending inbound rows to the transcript on the triggering `seq`. That drives the sidebar's `Clock` glyph, the sidebar's admission rule and the card's `PendingChip`, all from one derivation. It is real data and it is asymmetric by construction: **a request you SENT carries no state at all**
- ⚠ **THE TEMPTING WRONG FIX, named so nobody re-invents it:** reading "no pending row" as approved. The requester cannot see the row in EITHER state, so absence is indistinguishable from never-asked, from denied, and from expired — and a green check is a claim about a real person's decision. `components/channels-v2/bits.tsx › AddresseePill` therefore takes an OPTIONAL `approved` that no caller passes, and `transcript.test.tsx` pins that nothing renders an approval verdict
- **What a fix would need**, and it is a new projection, not a filter change: a requester-scoped read answering "for the threads I created, what is each target's consent status" — bounded to the requester's OWN threads, returning a status and nothing else (no `body_preview`, no `proposed_reply`, no requester identity beyond what the thread already exposes), and NOT reachable by naming another operator. ⚠ It widens who can see a consent decision, which §6 currently permits nobody to do; it is a **product + security decision, not a plumbing task**
- Related but distinct: wiring plan Phase 8 replaces the consent card with launch settings, which may change what a decision even is. Sequencing this before that ruling would build a projection over a model about to move
- ⚠ **UPDATE 2026-08-18 (Phase 8 shipped): the model did NOT move, so the blocker is unchanged.** The consent card became `components/launch-panel.tsx` and the decision became "Launch agent", but the ROW, its scoping and `requireOperatorRow` are byte-identical — INVARIANTS §6 now records that explicitly. **The addressee side gained a home** (`components/channels-v2/inbox-pane.tsx`, behind the sidebar's Inbox row); the requester side gained nothing, because there is still nothing to read. **The asymmetry is now visible in the product**, which makes the missing projection easier to notice and no easier to build
- Status: open (needs a ruling before a projection)

## F-207 — `channel_tasks_stale` outlived its only caller, and the drop is a migration this phase did not take (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 4 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md` (thread closing is removed), deleting `/api/cron/stale-threads`
- Location: `supabase/migrations/20260807160000_channel_tasks_stale_activity.sql › channel_tasks_stale`
- **The shape.** The stale sweep's whole body was a close PROPOSAL, so it went with thread closing (INVARIANTS §5, §13) — the route and `repository-tasks.ts › listStaleOpenThreads` were deleted in that change. **The RPC is still in the database.** Deleting the CALLER is not a migration; deleting the function is, so the code half was taken and this half was filed, exactly as the plan directs
- ⚠ **CORRECTION 2026-08-18 (wave-2 fix pass): this entry, INVARIANTS §13 and `repository-tasks.ts`'s own docblock all said the `vercel.json` entry went with the route. IT DID NOT.** `vercel.json` still listed `/api/cron/stale-threads` at `0 7 * * *`, so every deploy re-registered a schedule pointing at a route that no longer exists — a daily 404 with no end date, not the "harmless until the next deploy" that §13 asserted. The entry is deleted now; the three false statements are corrected in the same change. **The generalizable bit: a deletion that spans code AND config is only half-verifiable by `ls`, and the config half is exactly the half that gets claimed instead of checked**

- ✅ **It also closes out F-202** (two SQL expressions of one activity clock), which is deleted from this file. That finding's fear was drift between the RPC's lateral and `channel_tasks_activity`'s identical one. With no caller the RPC cannot disagree with anything — but it can still be READ as a live definition, and `supabase db reset` still replays it
- **What the drop looks like**, and it is one statement: `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS channel_tasks_stale(timestamptz, integer);`. ⚠ Verify the signature against the migration rather than this line — a `DROP FUNCTION` naming the wrong argument types is a no-op that reports success. ⚠ **`channel_tasks_activity` (`20260818120000`) is a DIFFERENT object and is load-bearing** — it is what `listTasksByChannel` reads. Do not delete it in the same breath

## F-209 — INVARIANTS §3 describes an `/authenticate` sign-in page and a loop-counted route set this tree does not have (2026-08-18) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-25

- Found during: Phase 4 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, while getting `node scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs` to a state where the phase's own doc edits could be checked
- **How it surfaced, and why that matters:** its dead symbol anchor — the §3 bullet named a `LOOP_COUNTED_AUTH_ROUTES` constant in `src/shared/auth/auth-routes.ts`, which holds no such symbol — was the **one pre-existing failure of that gate** — red at the phase's base commit and unrelated to anything in it. A single standing failure makes a gate useless for the next change, because "1 failure" and "1 failure plus mine" read the same at a glance
- **The disagreement, measured 2026-08-18.** §3 says the sign-in form is ONE page at `/authenticate` with `/login` and `/signup` as 307 redirectors, that all three are named in `AUTH_ENTRY_ROUTES`, and that the Q4 loop breaker counts `/login` and `/authenticate` together via `LOOP_COUNTED_AUTH_ROUTES`. In this tree: `ls src/app/authenticate` → no such directory; `src/shared/auth/auth-routes.ts › AUTH_ENTRY_ROUTES` is exactly `["/login", "/signup"]` and its docblock describes them as "ONE screen over two routes"; there is no `LOOP_COUNTED_AUTH_ROUTES` anywhere, and `shared/auth/login-bounce.ts` states the breaker is `/login`-only, with the reason (nothing redirects to `/signup`, so it cannot be one end of a cycle)
- **Why it is filed rather than fixed**, and it is the same call as F-208: the bullet is too specific and internally consistent to be invention, so either the `/authenticate` consolidation was reverted without the doc following, or the doc ran ahead of a branch. Deleting it would destroy the evidence; "restoring" the symbol to satisfy the checker is what the checker's own message forbids
- ⚠ **ADDENDUM, RESTORED 2026-08-18 (fix wave 3), sourced from Phase 8's independently-filed duplicate** (`git show wt/p8:docs/REFACTOR-FINDINGS.md`, where it was that worktree's F-207). The id was deduped at merge and the entry's TEXT was dropped with it; two points in it are not made anywhere else and are the reason the dedupe was lossy:
  - **THE TEMPTING WRONG FIX HAS TWO BRANCHES, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS A DOCS FIX.** Do not add the constant to `auth-routes.ts` to make the gate pass. Either the breaker really does count both paths under a different name — in which case REPOINT the anchor — or it does not, **in which case the §3 bullet was describing a guarantee the code does not provide, and that is a SECURITY-SHAPED CLAIM, not a docs typo.** Resolving this finding means saying which, out loud
  - **IT WAS FOUND TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, AS BACKGROUND NOISE.** Phase 8 hit it running the gate on a change that touched neither auth nor that section, and Phase 4 hit it separately. **A red gate that predates a change trains the next agent to skip the gate** — this one had been failing long enough that two phases each classified it as somebody else's problem before either recorded it. That is corroboration for the cost bullet above, not a restatement of it
- **What this pass DID do** (the minimum that makes the gate mean something again): the §3 bullet now opens with the measurement, quotes its own former claim as a claim, states what IS true of this tree, and carries no dead symbol anchor. The rule it protects — *never add a `redirect("/signup")`, because it puts an uncounted path at one end of a possible cycle* — is true either way and is stated unconditionally

What is genuinely wrong is that a doc describing uncommitted code was committed. Re-measure with `git status` in the main checkout; do not quote this
- **✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — THE SIDE THAT WAS STALE WAS THE COMMIT, AND IT LANDED.** The entry's own

## F-211 — Mentions are per-channel and unbackfilled, so a tag you have not clicked into is invisible (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 6 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, wiring the Tags inbox
- **Two gaps, both scoped-out deliberately, both worth naming before Phase 7 gates notifications on the same key:**
  - **NO WORKSPACE-WIDE MENTIONS SURFACE.** `GET /api/channels/[channelId]/mentions` answers for ONE channel, and the badge lives in that channel's Info tab. A message tagging you in a channel you have not selected raises nothing anywhere — the sidebar has no tags badge, and the only way to discover the tag is to click into the channel and open a disclosure. The read the projection is built on is already keyed `(channel_id, mentionedUserIds @> me)`; a workspace-wide variant is a different bound and a different clip wording, not a different query shape
  - **NO BACKFILL.** `metadata.mentionedUserIds` is stamped at INSERT, so every message written before this migration tags nobody, permanently. A backfill is possible in principle (re-parse stored bodies against each channel's CURRENT roster) and is the wrong thing to do casually: the roster has changed, so it would assert that somebody was tagged by a message written when they were not in the room — a fabricated claim about a real person's words, which is the same line the fixture era refused to cross
- **What is NOT a gap:** a mention arriving in the SELECTED channel is live, riding the `channel_messages` doorbell (`channel_mention_reads` is deliberately unpublished — INVARIANTS §7)
- Proposed resolution: take the workspace-wide read as its own piece of work, WITH the sidebar surface it feeds, and sequence it against Phase 7 — a notification policy gated on mentions and an inbox that only shows the open channel's are two halves of one product decision. Leave the backfill alone unless somebody rules on the roster-drift question
- ⚠ **SEQUENCING ANSWERED, AND NOT THE WAY THIS ENTRY PROPOSED: PHASE 7 SHIPPED FIRST (2026-08-18).** The notification is now gated on this same key while the inbox behind it is still per-channel, so the two halves are live out of order. **This raises the entry's severity rather than resolving any of it** — read F-212, which states the consequence precisely. Nothing here is fixed; the first bullet's "the only way to discover the tag is to click into the channel" is now also true of the only PUSH signal the desktop has
- Status: open


## ✅ F-212 — The agent view's direct 1:1 lane has no transport, so two of its three lanes are unbuilt (2026-08-18) — RESOLVED 2026-08-20

- Found during: Phase 5 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, wiring the Agents tab and the agent view. **CLOSED by the AGENT WINDOW**, which is the surface both missing lanes needed and which did not exist when this was filed
- **The entry's diagnosis was right on every count and is kept here rather than summarized**, because two of its three arguments decided how the fix was built:
  - ✅ **SENT — was already wired.** `components/channels-v2/agent-panel.tsx › agentSentMessages`. **The window IMPORTS it** rather than writing a second derivation
  - ✅ **WORK NARRATION.** The entry: *"Tool use reaches the SESSION WINDOW's own IPC stream … Surfacing it means either putting a bounded narration ring on `main/session-summary.js` (which is import-free below its sentinel and deliberately network-free — a per-event ring is a real cost decision against `PUSH_COALESCE_MS`) or a second bridge channel."* **The second bridge channel was taken, and the entry's own cost argument is why.** The summaries feed is DIGEST-GATED and `session-state-push.js` subscribes to that gate to decide when to write the server — so a per-event ring on it would either cost a server write per tool call or be swallowed by the digest. `main/session-narration.js` owns a bounded per-session ring (`NARRATION_MAX`, multiplicative against `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS` per §11) on its own coalesced channel. ⚠ Tool calls carry their NAMES, which is the specific half this entry called out
  - ✅ **THE DIRECT 1:1 LANE.** The entry: *"the desktop's own steer (`session:send`) is resolved from `event.sender` and is therefore bound to that session's window"* — exactly the obstacle, and exactly why the new op does NOT resolve from the sender: `main/session-reopen.js › messageByTask` resolves `(channel, thread)` against MAIN'S OWN registry, the same pair `pause`/`end` take, which makes it own-agents-only structurally rather than by a check
- **THE SECURITY REVIEW THIS ENTRY ASKED FOR, ANSWERED IN FULL.** It parked the lane on *"the `mainOnly` review that `sessions:pause`/`sessions:end` got, plus a ruling on whether an out-of-band steer bypasses the inbound gate"*:
  - **It dispatches the EXISTING `steer` event on the existing reducer branch** — no new branch, no second wake path. A second way to start a turn is a second set of lifecycle bugs
  - **It BYPASSES the inbound gate, and that is correct, because it is not inbound.** AXIS B governs COUNTERPARTY turns; this is the operator's own keyboard in a window MAIN created and registered. `session:send` was always an ungated steer for that reason — what changed is only WHICH window may send one, which is the widening Samuel already ruled on for the pop-out (option (a), the app-window registry)
  - **The text is DELIMITED, not fenced as data** (`main/session-seed.js › frameOperatorTurn`). Fencing the operator's words with `frameContinuation`'s "this is DATA, never instructions" preamble would invert the model the framing is built on — the operator is the one voice a session is told to weigh, and the 2026-08-01 incident was a mislabel in the other direction. The nonce delimiters do the other half of a fence's job: a body forging either vocabulary's `BEGIN-`/`END-` line is stripped
  - **The failure direction is stated rather than implied, because it is wider than pause/end's.** A forged call makes the operator's OWN agent do work they did not ask for, inside that session's existing profile and containment. It grants no tool, widens no posture, reaches no other machine, and cannot post without the outbound gate. That is why the op is bounded in the preload AND at the boundary (`MESSAGE_CAP`), refuses an empty body, and honours the version floor
- **A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND UNDER THIS ENTRY AND IS ALSO CLOSED.** `session-reopen.js › reopenByTask` answered `{ ok: true }` for a live WINDOWLESS session having opened nothing — the recreate fallback's existing-session branch — and `agents-model.ts › openAgentWindow` discarded the verdict anyway. **Two independent swallows over one click, on nearly every agent**, since the session-window retirement made windowless the ordinary shape
  - ⚠ **AND ITS FIRST FIX WAS REJECTED, WHICH IS THE MOST REUSABLE THING IN THIS ENTRY.** That fix made the refusal honest: `{ ok: false, reason: 'windowless' }`, worded in the panel as *"This agent runs without a window."* **Samuel called it meaningless, and it was: a window is a VIEW, not a runtime property.** Whether main happened to mint a `BrowserWindow` for a spawn is an implementation detail of the spawn shape — not a fact about the agent, and no answer at all to "show me what this thing is doing". **The lesson: an honest refusal is only worth shipping when the operator can DO something with it.** Reporting an internal reason beats silence and is not a substitute for the feature. The notice is deleted and the click always opens the view
- **What shipped:** `main/agent-window.js` (the window, `popout-window.js`'s shape and its inherited ruling), `main/session-narration.js` (the ring), `main/session-seed.js › frameOperatorTurn`, `session-reopen.js › messageByTask` + the windowless reopen branch, three bridge ops (`sessions.openAgentWindow` / `sessions.message` / `sessions.narration` + `onNarration`, each reviewed separately in `test/preload-parity.test.mjs › APP_OPS`), the SPA route + page, and `components/channels-v2/agent-window.tsx` with `› use-agent-narration.ts`
- **What did NOT come back: the session window.** It stays retired (F-228). This window has no transcript of its own, no permission cards, no folder chip and no modes header — those moved to the channels surfaces or died with the retirement. What it restores is the two things that were genuinely lost: watching one agent work, and saying something to it
- **✅ RE-VERIFIED AT THE CLOSE OF THE SESSION-WINDOW DELETION WAVE (2026-08-20), rather than taken on trust — all three lanes drive real code:** SENT is `channels-v2/agent-panel.tsx › agentSentMessages`, which the agent window IMPORTS rather than re-deriving; WORK NARRATION is `main/session-narration.js` → `channels-v2/use-agent-narration.ts` → `› agent-window.tsx`; the DIRECT 1:1 lane is `sessions.message` → `channel-dir-ipc.js › sessions:message` → `session-reopen.js › messageByTask`, `appWindowOnly`-bound like every op there
- ⚠ **ONE BUG WAS FOUND IN THAT RE-VERIFICATION AND FIXED, and it is the reusable half:** the deletion wave rebuilt `session-reopen.js › bind`'s `deps` literal and dropped `openAgentWindow` from it, so main passed the handle, `bind` discarded it, and every "Open window" click hit this module's own fail-closed guard. **A wiring bug and a correct refusal produced the same value** — only a test driving the WIRING, not the branch behind it, could tell them apart. `bind`'s docblock now states the rebuild rule
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-20). ⚠ The entry is kept rather than deleted because its cost argument for the second bridge channel, and the rejected-refusal lesson above, are both reusable and neither is recorded anywhere else

## F-213 — The mention gate is live before the surfaces that make an untagged message findable (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 7 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, wiring the notification policy
- Location: `dopl-desktop-app/main/targeting.js › mentionsMe` + `› classify`, `dopl-desktop-app/main/listener-messages.js › dispatchMessage`, `dopl-desktop-app/main/trigger.js › sendFyi`; the surfaces it depends on are `src/app/api/channels/[channelId]/mentions/**` and `src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/mentions-list.tsx`
- Severity: **smell, sequencing** — every individual piece is correct; what is missing is the half of the product that the retirement assumed
- **THE POLICY TRADED A PUSH SIGNAL FOR A PULL SURFACE, AND THE PULL SURFACE IS PER-CHANNEL (F-211).** Before this phase, an operator learned about a message they could see because the desktop told them. Now an untagged message raises nothing, and a TAGGED message in a channel that is not selected raises a banner that — if the app is closed, the OS suppressed it, or the operator was away — leaves the tag discoverable only by clicking into that channel and opening a disclosure. **The banner is not a record; the record is F-211's per-channel inbox.** The two were sequenced the other way round in F-211's proposed resolution and shipped in this order anyway
- **THE AGENT-SIDE HALF IS NOT BUILT EITHER, and it is the wiring plan's Phase 11.** "Tagging is a capability the agent must be TOLD it has" (MAPPING wiring intent) is MCP prose that does not exist yet, so until it lands **no agent tags anybody and the agent-escalation rate is zero**. That is the safe direction — the failure is silence, not noise — but it means the mention gate currently reads as "agents stopped notifying" rather than as "agents notify when it matters", and a judgement about whether the policy is right should not be formed on this interval
- **What was measured, not inferred:** the desktop's THREE remaining per-message notification paths are the addressed request (`consent.notifyInbound`, deliberately ungated), `trigger.js › sendFyi` and `task-notify.js › notifyTaskReply` (both gated). One concrete banner that used to fire and now does not: a peer's agent replying in an interactive thread opened by an EXTERNAL requester (the operator's own Claude Code over MCP). That reply still reaches the external session through its own armed await, so nothing is lost — but the desktop courtesy notice is gone unless the reply tags the operator (`test/wake-external-requester.test.mjs`, "EXTERNAL reply that tags NOBODY")
- Proposed resolution: do F-211's workspace-wide read and its sidebar badge as the next piece of channels work, and treat Phase 11's tagging prose as part of the same product decision rather than as MCP documentation. Do NOT answer this by widening the gate
## F-214 — A request notification lands on the channel, and the channel has no way to launch or decline (2026-08-18) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-30

- Found during: Phase 9 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, inverting the windowing
- Location: `src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/transcript.tsx › ThreadCardMessage` (the `PendingChip` branch) vs `src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/inbox-pane.tsx`
- **What the ruling asks for, and what the tree can do.** The ruling, from the port's intent doc (deleted at the Phase 12 cutover; the live statement is INVARIANTS §11): *notification click focuses the app and auto-navigates to the channel/DM where the request was made, **to launch or decline there***. The navigation half shipped. The **there** half did not: the v2 channel transcript renders a still-pending request as a `PendingChip` — a status, with no control — and the ONLY surface carrying a decision is the Inbox pane's `LaunchPanel`, which is a sidebar nav row away
- **So the operator's path is one click, not zero:** land on the channel → see the chip → open Inbox → launch or decline. The Inbox badge is visible on landing, so nothing is hidden; it is a step the ruling did not ask for
- **Why the phase did not "fix" it by routing requests to the Inbox instead.** The Inbox read is `(operator, workspace)`-scoped and WORKSPACE-WIDE by construction (F-206), so landing there discards the one fact the notification carried — which channel. It would also fork `targeting-window.js › openChannelForEntry`, the single seam all three notification producers share, on a distinction `entry` does not carry
- Proposed resolution: give the transcript's pending row a real decision control — the same `LaunchPanel`, inline, on the same `use-channel-preference-writes › consent` mutation and the same page-level `useRefetchGate` the Inbox pane already holds. That is a component placement, not a new read or a new write. ⚠ Do NOT solve it by making the chip a shortcut that opens the Inbox: that is the click this finding is about, wearing a different hat
- ⚠ **CLOSED 2026-08-30 — superseded BY RULING, not by the proposed fix.** Samuel retired the entire ask/answer vocabulary on 2026-08-22 (*"remove all the stuff about declining and approving of threads"*): `PendingChip`, the card's Decline/Launch pair, `ThreadAwaitingStrip` and the Inbox's inbound rows are all deleted, leaving `src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/thread-consent.tsx › ThreadSendBox` as the outbound-only survivor. **There is no inbound decision left to place on the channel** — so the one-click-not-zero cost this entry measured no longer exists to pay.
## F-215 — `prompt-framing.test.mjs` is 7 lines from the desktop's hard cap, and the desktop has zero exemptions (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 11 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, pinning the two new VOCABULARY capabilities on both sides
- Location: `dopl-desktop-app/test/prompt-framing.test.mjs` (measured `wc -l` = 493 on 2026-08-18, cap 500)
- **Why it is debt and not just a number.** INVARIANTS §1: the desktop's own `eslint.config.js` enforces `max-lines` 500 at `error` with **zero exemptions**, `skipComments: false`. This file is the prompt's prose pin — it grows every time a behaviour round rewrites a paragraph, which is exactly what Phase 11 did — so the next prose change is a SPLIT, done under time pressure, by whoever happens to be adding one assertion
- **The seam is not arithmetic and should be chosen now, not at the failure.** The file mixes three concerns that change for different reasons: FENCE/sanitization safety (nonce, forged BEGIN/END, id neutralization), the DELIVERY CALL's exact shape (the `task=` ban, the em-dash house rule, the thread tag), and the VOCABULARY / prose-invariant pins. The third is the one that grows, and it is the natural extraction — it would mirror the `prompt-framing.js` / `prompt-framing-text.js` split the source side already has
- Proposed resolution: extract the vocabulary + prose-invariant pins into `test/prompt-vocabulary.test.mjs` before the next prompt-copy change, not during it
