## F-216 — `CHANNEL_DESCRIPTION` has a hard budget for its LAW block and none at all for the other 90% (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 11 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, adding the sparse-post and @-tag teachings
- Location: `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-description.ts › CHANNEL_DESCRIPTION`; the guard that exists is `tools/channel-law.test.ts` ("keeps the law SHORT")
- **The asymmetry.** The LAW block is capped three ways — ≤8 bullets, ≤2200 chars total, ≤900 per bullet — with a comment explaining that it is read on every connection by every agent. **The rest of the description is read on exactly the same connections and is capped by nothing.** Measured 2026-08-18 off the built module: whole description 20,487 chars, of which the law is 1,951. Re-measure, do not quote:
  ```
  node -e "const d=require('./packages/mcp-server/dist/tools/channel-description.js').CHANNEL_DESCRIPTION; console.log(d.length)"
  ```
- **Phase 11 is the evidence, not the cause.** It added ~2.4k chars, all of it deliberately placed OUTSIDE the law precisely because the law is budgeted — which is the guard working as designed and also the shape of the problem: every phase that respects the law budget pushes its text into the unbudgeted majority. The op bullets are single lines of several thousand characters each
- **What a fix is NOT.** A total-character cap picked from today's size would be a number with no argument behind it, and the law's cap has one (it is read before anything else, so it competes with the agent's actual task). The honest version is per-SECTION: the conventions block and each op bullet answer "what does a caller of THIS op need", and a bullet that outgrows that is carrying guidance that belongs in the op's RESULT, where Phase 11 put both of its teachings
- Proposed resolution: decide whether the description has a budget at all before the next phase adds to it; if it does, cap the CONVENTIONS block and the per-op bullet separately, with the reasoning in the test as the law's cap has
- Status: open

## F-217 — Two pre-existing flaky tests intermittently red an otherwise-green suite (2026-08-18)

- Found during: the channels-v2 wiring waves — every long suite run risked one of these two, and both were measured AGAINST BASELINE commits to prove they predate the branch
- **`src/shared/version/latest-release.test.ts › "honours an injected clock"`** — first flagged by the Phase 1 pass, reproduced at the wave-2 join. ⚠ **THE RATE CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN, 2026-08-18 (fix wave 3): "roughly 1 run in 2..3, INCLUDING in isolation" is UNREPRODUCED.** That figure came from a 1-fail/2-run sample, which cannot support a rate at all. **Re-measured: 7 consecutive isolated runs of `npx vitest run src/shared/version/latest-release.test.ts`, 26/26 tests passing every time — 0 failures in 7.** The review that prompted the re-measure got 7/7 as well, independently. **What is still open is the MECHANISM, not the rate:** the file does hold a module-level cache read against an injected clock, and nobody has shown that shape is safe — a 0/7 sample no more proves determinism than 1/2 proved a coin flip. **Do not close this on the passing runs, and do not quote a rate in either direction; state the sample.** The honest status is "a suspicious shape with no current reproduction"
- **`apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/channels/index.test.tsx`** — fails ~40% under the FULL parallel suite, passes 4/4 in isolation; the Phase 3 pass measured the same rate at a pre-branch baseline worktree. Parallel-load shape, not a logic failure. (The Phase 5 pass saw the same contention pattern spread over channels/skills files in its worktree)
  - ⚠ **THE FILE WAS REWRITTEN AT THE PHASE 12 CUTOVER (2026-08-18)** — it mounted the deleted two-pane page and now mounts the three-column one, with a different transport mock. **Measured after the rewrite: 5 consecutive FULL parallel runs of `npm test -w @dopl/desktop-ui`, 25/25 files and 158/158 tests each time — no reproduction.** That is not a fix and must not be read as one: nobody changed the interleaving, the sample is small against a ~40% rate, and the OTHER half of this entry (`latest-release.test.ts`) is untouched and still flakes in isolation. Re-measure before closing
  - ✅ **THE SPA HALF IS REPRODUCED AGAIN, WITH A NAME, 2026-09-02 (Wave B slice B2).** Sample, stated per the rule above: **2 full `npm test -w @dopl/desktop-ui` runs, 1 failed** — `src/pages/channels/index.test.tsx:197`, `findByText("Picked it up, wiring the client queries now.")` timing out; the other run was 46/46 files and 433/433 tests clean. **Then 3 consecutive ISOLATED runs of that one file, 7/7 tests each, 0 failures** — which falsifies nothing, per the 2026-08-22 note, and is recorded only because it confirms the file is not broken on its own. **The branch touched no `apps/` file** (`git diff --stat` against the wave base lists 19 files, all `src/`), so it is neither caused nor masked by that work.
  - ⚠ **THE ASSERTION THAT TIMES OUT IS A `findByText`, WHICH IS THE SHAPE THIS ENTRY KEEPS DESCRIBING AND HAS NEVER NAMED.** `findBy*` is a `waitFor` with a fixed default timeout, so it converts "slow under parallel load" into "failed" with no other symptom — the same class as the `waitFor` at line 856 of this file, and the reason the two halves look alike under contention. **The output was redirected to a file, not piped, per this entry's own operational lesson**, which is the only reason the name survived this time.
- Cost: "1 failure" and "1 failure plus mine" read the same at a glance — the same argument F-209 made about a standing red gate applies to a COIN-FLIP gate
- Proposed resolution: the latest-release test needs its module-level cache reset (or injection) per test; the SPA page test likely needs its transport mock hardened against interleaving. Neither belongs to the channels branch; both are worth one quiet pass
- ⚠ **THE ENTRY'S OWN LESSON, TURNED ON ITSELF (2026-08-18, fix wave 3): BOTH HALVES OF THIS FINDING NOW CARRY A NUMBER NOBODY CAN REPRODUCE** — 5 clean full runs against the SPA test's "~40%", 7 clean isolated runs against the latest-release test's "1 in 2..3". A flake rate is a MEASUREMENT and obeys the same rule every other number in these docs does: it carries its sample and its date, or it is not written down. **Neither half is closed** — the shapes that would explain a flake are still in both files, and an unreproduced flake is the one kind of bug that looks fixed for free
- ✅ **REPRODUCED 2026-08-22 (v1.17.1 cross-lane verification), and the shape is narrower than this entry assumed.** Sample, stated per the rule above: **4 full `npm test` runs at the root, 2 failed** — both on `latest-release.test.ts:316 › "honours an injected clock, so the TTL is testable without a timer stub"`, both `expect(spy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` with `Number of calls: 1`, i.e. the scheduled refresh fired one tick EARLY. The other two runs were 221 files / 3140 tests clean. **In the same session, 1 isolated run of `npx vitest run src/shared/version/latest-release.test.ts` passed 26/26.**
  - ⚠ **THE ISOLATION RESULT AND THE FULL-SUITE RESULT ARE DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS, AND THIS ENTRY HAS BEEN CONFLATING THEM.** The withdrawn "1 in 2..3 INCLUDING in isolation" claim was retired on 7 clean ISOLATED runs — but isolation is the condition under which it does not fail. Both halves of F-217 now look like **the same parallel-load shape**, which is what the SPA half was always described as; the module-level cache is a plausible amplifier under contention rather than an independent cause. **Re-measure with the full suite, never in isolation** — an isolated run of this file cannot falsify anything.
  - This wave did not touch the file (`git status` clean for it) and the failure reproduces on the merged tree exactly as described, so it is neither caused nor masked by v1.17.1.
- ⚠ **OBSERVED AGAIN 2026-08-25 (the outbound-review + right-pane wave), AND THE NAME WAS NOT CAPTURED — which is itself the note.** Sample, stated per the rule above: **~15 full `npm run test` runs at the root over the session, 2 reported `1 failed | 3721 passed`**, then **11 consecutive green**, including a deliberate 7-run capture loop that never reproduced. Both failures landed on runs whose output was piped through `tail`, so the failing spec scrolled past and no name survives. **The rate (~13%) and the "one test, full-suite only, never on demand" shape match this entry's root half**, but nothing here ATTRIBUTES them to it — an unnamed failure attributed by resemblance is how a real second flake gets absorbed into an existing entry and stops being looked for.
  - **The operational lesson, cheap and worth keeping: never `| tail` a suite run you might need to diagnose.** Redirect to a file and tail the file. This session lost two reproductions to a pipe.
- Status: open (both halves — the latest-release half now HAS a reproduction under full-suite parallelism, 2/4 on 2026-08-22; mechanism still unexplained)

## F-218 — The historical agent-attribution READER is gone; the key it protects is now reserved with nothing rendering it (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 12 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, the cutover — the finding is a CONSEQUENCE of the demolition, not a bug in it
- **What went.** `channel-transcript.tsx` was the only reader of `lib/agent-display.ts` (`agentAttributionFor`), which was the only reader of `hooks/use-channel-agents.ts`, which was the only client caller of `GET /api/channels/[channelId]/agents`. Deleting the two-pane page orphaned all three; `npx knip` named the hook and the chain was walked from there. All three are deleted
- **What that costs, precisely.** A message stored before the named-agent rollback carries `metadata.author_agent_id` and used to render "quartz · Ada's agent". The v2 transcript never resolved that key — it labels an agent post off `authorKind` (INVARIANTS §5) — so those rows now render as the OPERATOR's name plus an "Agent" chip. **A display simplification, not a data loss:** the column is untouched and the projection still returns it
- ⚠ **THE STRIP LIST DID NOT CHANGE, AND MUST NOT BE "CLEANED UP" ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS ENTRY.** INVARIANTS §5 keeps `author_agent_id` / `to_agent_id` / `to_agent_ids` in `service-writes-metadata.ts › resolvePostMetadata`'s delete run on the rule "a key stays reserved with no writer only while something still RENDERS it" — and its own corollary, "a reader coming back means the key comes back to the strip list FIRST". Removing the strip is a WIDENING: it makes the key caller-settable, so the day a reader returns, so does the forgery. The §5 bullet was corrected in this change to say the reader is GONE rather than that it exists; the reservation stays
- **Left behind, deliberately un-deleted:** the route `src/app/api/channels/[channelId]/agents/route.ts` and `src/features/channels/server/service-reads.ts › listAgents` behind it. Removing an API surface is not a renderer deletion and was out of this phase's scope; it is also the read a future attribution surface would use
- Proposed resolution: decide whether historical agent attribution is a product requirement. If yes, resolve `author_agent_id` in `channels-v2/view-model-rows.ts › toMessageRow` off a channel-scoped roster read and restore the two deleted modules from git. If no, retire the route and the service read in one change — and leave the strip list alone either way
- Status: open (question — the code state is deliberate and consistent; what is undecided is whether the attribution should come back)

## F-219 — A non-member public channel is listed with a live composer and no join affordance (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 12 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, checking what the deleted page did that the new one does not
- `server/service-reads.ts › listChannels` returns public channels the caller has NOT joined (`repo.listChannels` takes `memberChannelIds` plus the public set), so such a channel appears in `components/channels-v2/sidebar.tsx`'s tree. The retired `channel-pane.tsx` branched on `channel.isMember` and rendered a "You are viewing this public channel / Join channel" card in place of the composer; **`channels-v2/message-pane.tsx` renders `ChannelsV2Composer` unconditionally**
- So the operator can type and press send into a channel they are not in. The server refuses it, which makes this a UI-truthfulness bug rather than an authorization one — but "compose, send, watch it fail" is the shape the join card existed to prevent
- ⚠ **PRE-DATES THE CUTOVER.** The v2 surface shipped without the branch through Phases 2–9; the cutover is what made it the shipping behaviour. The `join` / `leave` writes both survive (`hooks/use-channel-lifecycle-writes.ts`), and `leave` IS reachable from the new header's kebab — only `join` has no caller
- Proposed resolution: restore the branch in `message-pane.tsx` — `isMember ? <Composer/> : <JoinCard/>` — wired to `lifecycle.join`. Small, and it is the last un-called write in that hook
- Status: open

## F-220 — `channels-skeleton.tsx` draws a two-pane page the product no longer has (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 12 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, the cutover
- `components/channels-skeleton.tsx` composes `TwoPaneListSkeleton` + `DetailPaneSkeleton`, and its docblock said so — it was built for the master/detail page that the cutover deleted. It is still the initial-load branch of `channels-v2/channels-v2-core.tsx`, which paints THREE columns (tree · transcript · info panel)
- Cost is small and entirely cosmetic: the first paint reflows when live data arrives, which is the one thing a skeleton exists to prevent
- ⚠ **Do not fix it by hand-rolling a recipe in the channels tree.** The file's own docblock records that it used to carry a local `animate-pulse` / `bg-surface-raised-2` clone and that `shared/ui/skeleton.tsx` plus DESIGN-SYSTEM.md forbid exactly that. A third column is a third shared primitive, or one added to the kit
- Proposed resolution: add the info-panel column from the shared kit, or retire the skeleton for the empty-tree render the surface already has
- Status: **open — RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-30 and STILL VALID, and how it nearly closed is the useful half**
- ⚠ **A 2026-08-30 pass classified this SUPERSEDED and was WRONG, by resolving the FILENAME against the
  wrong tree.** There are two files called `channels-skeleton.tsx`:
  `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/channels/channels-skeleton.tsx`, which the skeleton wave DID rebuild, and
  `src/features/channels/components/channels-skeleton.tsx`, **which this entry names** and which still
  composes `TwoPaneListSkeleton` + `DetailPaneSkeleton` while `channels-v2/channels-v2-core.tsx` still
  paints it. **Two same-named files in two trees, one fixed and one not, is precisely the shape that
  makes an entry look closed to a reader who greps a basename** — treat any such claim as unverified
  until the TREE is named, not just the file.
- ⚠ **AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THIS ENTRY DESCRIBES: THE PAGE PAINTS TWO DIFFERENT SKELETONS IN SEQUENCE.**
  The wrong-shaped one above is the initial-load branch; a second, correctly-shaped one follows it as the
  live read settles. So the first paint reflows into a skeleton and then reflows again into content —
  the reflow this entry calls "small and entirely cosmetic" happens twice. The fix is one `loadingSkeleton`
  slot, not two skeletons that agree.

## F-221 — ✅ RESOLVED: copies of the IPC sender guard disagreed, with the more privileged ones on the lenient side (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 10 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, widening the sender binding to the app-window registry
- ⚠ **THERE ARE THREE COPIES, NOT TWO, AND THE MISCOUNT IS THE FINDING'S SECOND HALF** (see the update at the end). The tree keeps them on purpose — `main/ui-bridge.js` (which REJECTS), `main/channel-dir-ipc.js` (which returns each op's own refusal value, and whose pure block is sliced by `test/channel-ipc-sender.test.mjs`, so de-duplicating it would break the test that guards it), and `main/update-required-window.js › isGateSender` (window-identity rather than registry)
- **They did not agree.** ui-bridge read `if (!frame || !sender.mainFrame || frame !== sender.mainFrame) return false` — fail-closed on a `senderFrame` reading as null/undefined. channel-dir-ipc read `if (frame && sender.mainFrame && frame !== sender.mainFrame) return false` — which **waved that case through**
- ⚠ **The divergence ran the wrong way.** channel-dir-ipc is the more privileged of the two files: it is where `channels:setPermissionPreset` arms the permission posture a spawned agent runs with (the H3 HIGH), and where `sessions:reopen` / `threads:openWindow` mint windows
- Not known to be exploitable — Electron supplies `senderFrame` for a live frame, and the detached case already threw and was caught — so this is a latent hole rather than a live one, which is why it was closed rather than filed and left
- **Resolved in the same security change**, because that change was already re-deriving both predicates and leaving one lenient would have been a deliberate choice nobody made. Both are fail-closed on an absent frame now, and `channel-ipc-sender.test.mjs` has a case named for this id
- ⚠ **A THIRD COPY WAS FOUND STILL LENIENT (2026-08-18, wave-2 fix pass), AND THE REASON IS THIS ENTRY'S OWN COUNT.** `main/update-required-window.js › isGateSender` carried the exact pre-Phase-10 form. It was missed because both this finding and INVARIANTS §11 said "two copies" and named the two, so the search that would have found the third was never run — **an enumeration in a doc is a search nobody repeats.** The window it guards is not a minor one: its live ops are `update-gate:act` (restart) and `update-gate:quit`, both of which end the process, and it is deliberately OUTSIDE the app-window registry (a blocking screen must not hold the app's privileged surface), which is exactly why it has its own copy and why the registry-scoped review did not sweep it
- **Closed the same way**, and now driven rather than grepped: `test/update-required-screen.test.mjs` slices the real `isGateSender` and executes it, with a case named for this id. All three copies are byte-consistent on the frame branch
- Status: RESOLVED (kept as the record of why the three copies are now byte-comparable, and of the standing hazard, which just proved itself: **N copies of one predicate drift, nothing lints that, and a doc that states N is how the N+1th stays invisible**)

## F-222 — ui-sync watches ONE workspace, last-writer-wins, now that more than one window can ask (2026-08-18)

- Found during: Phase 10 of `docs/CHANNELS-V2-WIRING-PLAN.md`, widening the realtime doorbell to the app-window registry
- `main/ui-sync.js` holds ONE realtime channel, joined with `filter: workspace_id=eq.{watched}`, and `dopl:sync-watch` sets `watched` for whichever renderer called last. That was exactly right while there was one window
- With a POP-OUT open it is last-writer-wins: both windows normally view the same workspace (the pop-out is opened from the main window's own channel), so nothing is visible day to day — but **switching workspaces in the main window while a pop-out is open leaves the pop-out's workspace unwatched**, and the pop-out's transcript then stops updating with no error and nothing in its log. The renderer's registry filters incoming events by `workspaceId`, so the mismatched frames it does receive are dropped rather than misapplied — the failure is staleness, not wrong data
- Phase 10 did the cheap honest half: `watch()` now logs the transition by NAME (`the watched workspace MOVED while windows were open`) rather than making it silent, and `start()`'s docblock states the bound
- Proposed resolution: make `watched` a SET keyed by sender `webContents.id` and join one channel per distinct workspace (realtime binds one filter per table per channel, so a union is genuinely more than one channel — this is not a filter change). Bound it: the app-window budget is small, so the channel count is too
- ⚠ Do NOT "fix" it by dropping the `workspace_id` filter and letting the renderer sort it out. The filter is what keeps the CDC evaluation scoped, and the whole reason this feed exists is that per-component channels ate >80% of DB time
- Status: open

## F-223 — `src/shared/supabase/types.ts` is HAND-MAINTAINED with no generation script, and nothing detects the drift (2026-08-18)

- Found during: the wave-2 fix pass over the channels-v2 review findings, patching the two 2026-08-18 schema objects into the generated types
- **The shape.** The file is `supabase gen types typescript` OUTPUT in form — `Database`, `__InternalSupabase.PostgrestVersion`, the Row/Insert/Update/Relationships shape — but **no script in the tree regenerates it.** `package.json` has no `gen:types` / `supabase gen` entry (measured 2026-08-18, `grep -n 'gen types\|gen:types' package.json`), so every schema change since whenever it was last generated has had to be hand-carried, and two were not
- **What was missing**, both from migrations dated the same day the review ran: `channel_mention_reads` (`20260818140000`, a TABLE) and `channel_tasks_activity` (`20260818120000`, a VIEW — which `repository-tasks.ts › listTasksByChannel` reads on every channel open). Both were hand-added in this pass, in the file's own style
- ⚠ **NOTHING TYPE-ERRORED EITHER WAY, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL FINDING.** The channels repository goes through `supabaseAdmin()`, which is **untyped**, so `db.from("channel_tasks_activity")` compiled fine against a `Database` that had never heard of it. The generated types are therefore documentation with no enforcement behind it on this path — a table can be added, renamed or dropped and both typechecks stay green. That predates this branch and was deliberately left alone here
- ⚠ **`agent_trust_rules` STAYS DECLARED TOO, on exactly the same terms (added 2026-08-22).** The table is DROPPED by `20260822140000_retire_inbound_consent_and_trust.sql` (INVARIANTS §6), which is WRITTEN AND NOT APPLIED — so a real `gen types` run against the live project would still emit it, and hand-deleting it would make the file diverge from generation in order to look tidier. **It goes when that migration is applied and the types are regenerated, not before.** Second worked example of the bullet below, and the second time this entry's absence of a generator has meant a schema change is carried in prose instead of in the artifact
- ⚠ **`channel_tasks_stale` STAYS DECLARED, and that is correct rather than stale.** The review listed it as drift; it is not. F-207 records that the FUNCTION IS STILL IN THE DATABASE with no caller — dropping it is an unwritten migration — so a real `gen types` run today would still emit it. **Deleting it from the types would have made the file diverge from generation in order to look tidier.** It goes when F-207's migration goes
- ⚠ **The hand-patch is a patch, not a generation, and two details are guesses:** the view's `Relationships` is written `[]` (the generator's inference for a view over a lateral join is not reproducible by reading the file), and every view column is typed nullable, as the generator does for non-updatable views. **Re-derive both from a real run rather than from these lines**
- Proposed resolution: add a `gen:types` script (`supabase gen types typescript --project-id <ref> > src/shared/supabase/types.ts`) and either a CI check that regenerating produces no diff, or — since only a linked project can answer — a documented step in the migration ritual. **Whichever: the current state is a generated artifact with no generator, which is the same class as F-203's tracked `dist` with no rebuild gate**
- Status: open (needs a script + a decision about enforcement, not a patch)

## F-224 — `check-doc-refs` had two blind spots, and the channels-v2 review walked through both (2026-08-18) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-30

- Found during: the channels-v2 adversarial review, whose two largest classes of finding were BOTH invisible to the one gate that exists to catch exactly them (`node scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs`, INVARIANTS §14)
- **BLIND SPOT ONE — `.md` was not in `SOURCE_EXT`.** The file-reference and symbol-anchor regexes both build off that alternation, so a doc naming another doc was never checked in either form. The review found **42 live citations of `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/channels-v2/MAPPING.md`** across ~20 source files and 4 docs, months-fresh in tone and pointing at a file DELETED at the Phase 12 cutover, all of them green
- ⚠ **AND FIXING THE EXTENSION DOES NOT FIX THE 42, WHICH IS THE SHARPER HALF.** `md` is in `SOURCE_EXT` now (this change), so a markdown path carrying a `:NNN` line number, or a markdown path carrying a `›` symbol anchor, are both checked now (spelled out rather than shown, because a literal example here would be checked too — the extension caught this entry's own first draft) — but **every one of those 42 was a BARE PATH**, no `:NNN` and no `›`, and a bare-path class is deliberately still not implemented: `its intent lived in a MAPPING.md next to it` is prose, and a checker with false failures gets switched off, which costs more than this gap. **So the class that actually rotted is still uncovered, and this entry is the record of that decision rather than of a fix.** Anyone building it should start from "a bare path inside a code span, in a live (non-`DATED_CAPTURES`) doc" and measure the false-positive rate before wiring it to an exit code
- **BLIND SPOT TWO — `F-NNN` ids were only ever scanned inside `docs/*.md`.** The review found **five source files citing `F-203` where they meant `F-206`** (`view-model-requested.ts`, `› .test.ts`, `transcript.tsx`, `› .test.tsx`, `bits.tsx`) plus a migration citing `F-201` where it meant `F-207`. **Class (d) is added here** — the same resolve-or-fail rule over `src/`, `packages/`, `apps/`, `dopl-desktop-app/`, `scripts/`, `supabase/`. Measured on the way in: **1577 files scanned, 420 F-id references outside `docs/`, 0 unresolved**, so it landed green rather than with a backlog (~0.3 s for the whole run)
- ⚠ **STATE THE CEILING SO NOBODY MISTAKES A PASS FOR A PROOF, and it is the SAME ceiling class (b) already had: this catches a DANGLING id, never a MIS-CITED one.** `F-203` is a live entry. Every one of the six mis-cites this finding exists because of **would still pass under the new class** — they were fixed by a human reading them, and the check would only have fired if `F-203` had been deleted as resolved. What class (d) buys is the OTHER direction: the log's convention is that a resolved entry is DELETED, so an id cited from code is one prune away from meaning nothing, and until now nothing noticed
- **The generalizable bit, and it is the reason to keep this entry after the code change:** a gate's SCOPE is a claim about where a class of rot can occur, and this one's scope had been inherited from its first day (`docs/*.md`, non-recursive) through three later hardenings that each widened what it checked and never re-asked WHERE. **A checker that is green over the wrong tree reads exactly like a checker that is green.**
- Fixed in this change: `md` in `SOURCE_EXT`; class (d) over the six source roots, with `dist/` skipped there and only there (generated output carries whatever its source carried, so an id in it is not a second claim); the run now prints the source-tree counts beside the doc counts, because a scope you cannot see in the output is a scope nobody re-asks
- Status: open (the two extensions LANDED; the bare-path class is measured, argued and deliberately NOT taken — that half is what stays open)
- ⚠ **CLOSED 2026-08-30 — superseded:** the open half — the deliberately-untaken bare-path class — shipped 2026-08-26 as class (e) in `scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs › PLAIN_PATH_BASELINE_REL`, a MEASURED RATCHET over `scripts/doc-refs-plain-path-baseline.json`. What remains open is the baselined debt, which is **F-337**, not this.
- ⚠ **AND THE NUMBER THAT GETS QUOTED FOR IT IS WRONG.** The baseline file records `measuredAt 2026-08-26`, **`count` 457** (and 457 `entries`), with **613** as `rawViolationsAtMeasurement`. The "611 baselined refs" quoted in `docs/DRIFT-LEDGER-2026-08-30.md` matches neither number; the baselined count is **457**.


## F-226 — a per-file line cap is not a property either side of a MERGE can be checked for (2026-08-18)

- Found during: F-225's fix (the split that took `view-model.ts` back under the cap). **This entry is F-225's other half**, split off rather than deleted with it — the split closed the line count; nothing closed the way the line count got there
- **The mechanism, measured on F-225 with `git show <commit>:<path> | wc -l`:** `components/channels-v2/view-model.ts` was **416** at Phase 5 (`4daa2eba`), **427** at review-fix wave 1 (`b19b4fdc`) and **497** at wave 2 (`e35245e0`) — under cap at every one — and **508** at the wave-2 MERGE (`202935e4`), which took wave 2's additions on one side and the cutover/Phase-10 additions on the other. **Neither parent violated the cap and the merge result did**, so every branch tip was green and the tree was red
- **Why no gate saw it.** The `src/` half of the 500-line cap is enforced by eslint alone (INVARIANTS §1) and `size-check` in ci.yml covers `packages/` only, so the cap is only as reliable as somebody running lint on the MERGE RESULT. CI lints what it is given; the parallel-worktree workflow this repo now uses routinely produces a merge commit nobody lints before it lands
- **What would fix it:** lint the merge commit rather than the branch tip — a merge queue, or a required check that runs on the merge result. **The cheap interim is a habit, not a config:** `npx eslint .` immediately after any multi-worktree merge, before the merge is pushed. ⚠ Do NOT "fix" it with an `eslint.config.mjs` exemption; that list carries "DO NOT ADD TO THIS LIST — split the file instead"
- **The generalizable bit:** a per-file threshold — line cap, bundle budget, coverage floor — is checkable on a commit and NOT composable across a merge. Two changes that each fit can add up to one that does not, and every gate in the pipeline will have passed. Same class as F-224's lesson about a gate's SCOPE: green over the wrong tree reads exactly like green
- ⚠ **IT HAPPENED AGAIN, TO A DIFFERENT FILE, WITHIN TWO DAYS (measured 2026-08-20 at `c40b373f`).** `npx eslint .` over the root tree reported exactly one problem: `components/channels-v2/channels-v2-core.tsx` at **503 lines**. **The root lint gate was RED at `HEAD` before this session touched anything** — which is the part worth recording, because the entry above predicted a merge and this was a plain sequence of small additions to a file whose own docblock said *"this file sits a handful of lines inside the 500-line cap"*. **A comment is not a gate**, and a file that advertises how little headroom it has is a file every subsequent change spends the last of it on. Closed by a SPLIT on the seam its own siblings already use (`use-inline-consent.ts`, `use-agents-panel.ts`, `derivations.ts`): the eight pieces of selection/nav state plus the render-time `initialChannelId` re-application moved to `components/channels-v2/use-channels-v2-selection.ts`, taking the core to **454**. `ChannelsV2Core`, `› onCreated` and `› openMention` deliberately STAYED — all three are cited from `docs/` and a split that moves a cited symbol is a doc edit wearing a refactor's clothes
- **What the second instance adds to the diagnosis:** the interim habit this entry proposed (`npx eslint .` after a merge) would NOT have caught this one — there was no merge. The honest interim is narrower and duller: **`npx eslint .` before any commit that grows a file already over ~470**, and never trusting a docblock's account of its own headroom. The real fix is still a required check on the merge/HEAD result
- ⚠ **AND A THIRD MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD WORRY THE NEXT READER (2026-08-20).** Four files now sit at or one line under the cap: `dopl-desktop-app/main/session-engine.js` **500**, `dopl-desktop-app/main/session-summary.js` **500**, `components/channels-v2/channels-v2-core.tsx` **500**, `components/channels-v2/agents-tab.test.tsx` **498** (`wc -l`, 2026-08-20 — re-measure, do not quote). **Zero headroom is not "passing"; it is the state immediately before the failure this entry is about**, and three of those four reached it by ADDING VALUE (a require, a wired prop, a reviewed comment) rather than by bloat
  - **The engine's 500 is deliberate and load-bearing** — its two 2026-08-20 additions were paid for by JOINING existing lines, so the file is at cap BY CONSTRUCTION and any future edit there must budget a line first. That is a real technique and not a trick, but it only works while somebody remembers to use it
  - ⚠ **RE-MEASURED 2026-08-20, AND THE SHAPE IS NOW CLEAR ENOUGH TO NAME.** `main/channel-dir-ipc.js` **500**, `components/channels-v2/channels-v2-core.tsx` **500**, `components/channels-v2/agents-tab.test.tsx` **498** — while `session-engine.js` (473) and `session-summary.js` (461) came DOWN, because both were split on the seams this entry named. **The splits work; what does not is that nothing schedules them.** Four more were taken under time pressure in one session (`session-metrics.js`, `agents-controls.ts`, `agent-posture.tsx`, `sidebar-disclosure.test.tsx`), each one correct and each one decided at the moment a lint failed rather than when the seam appeared
- **What actually costs the lines is this tree's own review discipline**, which is the tension worth naming: a widened parity pin REQUIRES a reviewed-add comment, and those comments are 10–20 lines. Twice in one session a required comment did not fit and forced a file split (`session-summary.test.mjs` → `session-summary-shape.test.mjs`) or a consolidation (`agents-tab.test.tsx`'s open-agent case → `agents-detail.test.tsx`). **Both were the right outcome and neither was planned**, which means the cap is currently doing test-suite architecture by accident
  - **The seams to take FIRST, named now rather than under time pressure:** `channels-v2-core.tsx`'s two workspace-scoped overlays (the agent panel + the create dialogs) are a coherent "overlays" group with no reads of their own; `session-summary.js`'s live half (registry, ledger, ended set, push) is a different reason-to-change from its pure projection, and the harness already slices exactly that boundary
- ⚠ **A FOURTH MEASUREMENT, AND THE FIRST ONE WHERE THE SEAMS WERE TAKEN ON PURPOSE (2026-08-20, the audit-execution pass).** Three files sat at EXACTLY 500 — `main/channel-dir-ipc.js`, `test/session-summary.test.mjs`, `test/session-auth-recovery.test.mjs` — and **the audit found what a file AT the cap actually costs, which this entry had not stated: `channel-dir-ipc.js` was carrying FOUR stale docblocks, including a SECURITY-MODEL paragraph still describing the main window as hosting remote usedopl.com content, and under INVARIANTS §1 it could not absorb the correction.** A file at the cap does not merely stop growing; **it stops being correctable**, and the corrections it blocks are exactly the ones a future reader acts on
  - **All three were split on the seam, and each seam was reason-to-change rather than line count.** `channel-dir-ipc.js` → per-channel SETTINGS stays, the `sessions:*` / `threads:*` AGENT+WINDOW ops move to `main/session-ipc-ops.js` (500 → 173 + 339). `session-summary.test.mjs` → §4, the ended retention rule, to its own suite (it was the half F-234 needed to grow). `session-auth-recovery.test.mjs` → §4, the H1 engine-understands-the-hold cases, to their own suite (the half that drives the reducer end to end, so every new wake path lands there)
  - **Two shared harnesses came out of it rather than two copies of a loader** (`_ipc-harness.mjs`, `_auth-hold-harness.mjs`), on the `_classify-harness.mjs` precedent. ⚠ **`channel-ipc-sender.test.mjs` crossed the cap DURING the split**, because reading two sources instead of one is what a split costs its suite — the harness is what took it back under, and copying the loader instead would have been two suites booting two different programs
  - **The structural belt was widened with the split, not after it:** the "no handler skips the wrapper" check reads BOTH sources concatenated, so an op that dodges the binding fails whichever half it was added to. **That is the property a split must not cost, and it is the thing most likely to be forgotten** — a per-file assertion silently narrows its own scope when the file divides
- Status: open (process/CI; no code change closes it. The splits are still symptom fixes — but the 2026-08-20 batch was scheduled by the audit rather than by a lint failure, which is the first time this entry's own advice was followed rather than recorded)

## F-227 — four places cite an `isLifecycleEcho` symbol in `view-model.ts`; this tree has never had one (2026-08-18)

- Found during: F-225's split, chasing every `view-model.ts` anchor that the move would relocate. This one could not be relocated, because it resolves nowhere: `grep -rn "isLifecycleEcho" src packages apps docs` finds **four CITATIONS and zero definitions**. ⚠ Every citation below is named in PROSE, never written in the docs' `path` + `›` + `symbol` form — this file is itself checked, so an entry that shows the broken anchor fails the gate it is reporting (the same dodge F-224's entry had to take)
- **Where it is cited:** `src/features/channels/server/errors.ts`, `src/features/channels/server/service-writes-lifecycle-guard.test.ts`, `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-lifecycle-kinds.test.ts` and `docs/ENGINEERING.md` (the *"the desktop could stop POSTING the three runtime kinds"* section). The function they mean is `isLifecycleKind`, which now lives in `components/channels-v2/view-model-rows.ts`
- ⚠ **THE NAME IS THE SMALLER HALF. THE CLAIM ATTACHED TO IT IS STALE TOO**, and it is stale in the direction that matters: all four say the reader "drops the three kinds on sight", which stopped being true at the wave-2 fix pass — `toReceiptRow` now renders `task_finished`/`task_failed` as a receipt line and drops only `task_started` (INVARIANTS §5). So an answer posted as `task_finished` does not render NOWHERE, which is the exact sentence `errors.ts` uses to justify its 403. **The rule the 403 enforces is still right; the rendering fact it cites is not.**
- **Why nothing caught it, and there are TWO reasons, one of them new.** (i) Class (c) symbol anchors are resolved in `docs/` ONLY — the source-tree pass F-224 added checks `F-NNN` ids and nothing else — so the three SOURCE citations were never in scope. (ii) The fourth is in `docs/ENGINEERING.md`, which is in scope and is not a `DATED_CAPTURES` doc, and it passes anyway: **the docs are scanned LINE BY LINE** (`scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs`, `lines.forEach`) and that citation is hard-wrapped mid-anchor — the `›` is the last character of its line and `isLifecycleEcho` is the first word of the next. `SYMBOL_ANCHOR_RE`'s symbol half is `[^\n\`]+`, which needs at least one character after the `›` on the SAME line, so the anchor is not seen at all. Verified 2026-08-18 by running the regex against that line
- ⚠ **THAT IS A THIRD BLIND SPOT IN THE SAME CHECKER, AND IT IS F-224'S CLASS EXACTLY: a gate green over the wrong TEXT reads like a gate green.** Every anchor in `docs/` that a paragraph wrap happens to break after the `›` is unchecked, and nothing about the doc looks different. Fixing it is one line (scan the doc as one string with the `s` flag, or rejoin wrapped lines before matching) plus a re-measure of what that newly catches — do the measure first, since these docs wrap constantly and the backlog could be large
- **The fix, when taken:** repoint all four at `view-model-rows.ts › isLifecycleKind` AND rewrite the rendering claim in the same edit — repointing alone promotes a stale fact onto a live anchor, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md's precedence rule exists to prevent. Widening class (c) to the source trees is the separate, larger question F-224 left open
- Status: open (deliberately not fixed inside F-225's split, which was a MOVE — every export kept its name and signature, and rewriting a lifecycle claim in four files is a different change with a different reviewer question)

## ✅ F-228 — the session-window machinery is unreachable code awaiting deletion (2026-08-20) — RESOLVED 2026-08-20

- Found during: Samuel's two-account live test of channels v2 (1.11.1). The sender's own thread opener minted a v1 SESSION WINDOW on the sender's machine and launched their agent against their own message; the addressee's reply was then held at that window's inbound gate as "Message waiting". The fix RETIRED window mode outright — `getWindowMode()` answers false unconditionally (INVARIANTS §11), the tray toggle and "Sessions" submenu are deleted, and `classify`'s task-reply suppression widened to every author kind and mode (INVARIANTS §5)
- **✅ EXECUTED 2026-08-20, in two waves.** WAVE 0 moved the four things the deletion would otherwise have taken with it; WAVE 1 deleted the lane. The order was the whole point and is the reusable part:
  - **THE MOVES CAME FIRST, AND THEY WERE NOT OPTIONAL.** `session-window.js` exported `{ createSessionWindow, lifecycleHandlers }` and `index.js` wired BOTH — the second is the calm `task_progress {session_ended}` note that tells a WAITING PEER this machine stopped, which §11's quit guard depends on and which a WINDOWLESS session raises exactly as a windowed one did. A plain `rm` would have removed peer notification with no error anywhere. Likewise `trigger-headless.js`'s `RESEND` / `AUTH_HELD_REPLY` (consumed by `trigger.js` on the surviving windowless path), the SPA's `PermissionPreset` vocabulary (imported by the DURABLE posture, which outlives the arm), and `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS`. **Three of those four sat in a file the sweep was about to delete and were about something else entirely.**
  - **DELETED WHOLE:** `renderer/session/**` (19 files, 4,773 lines), `main/session-window.js`, `session-shell.js`, `session-ipc.js`, `session-consent.js`, `session-replay.js`, `session-peer-post.js`, `session-history.js`, `session-history-copy.js`, `attended-handoff.js`, `attended-prompt.js`
  - **CUT DOWN, NOT DELETED** (each kept every rule that was not about a window): `session-gate.js` lost the hold/accept family (`decideInbound`, `drainQueue`, `drainInbound`, `feedInboundForTask`) and its banner (`windowHasFocus`, `notifyInbound`, `surface`); `session-park.js` lost the shell-recreate family whole and kept the RESUME family; `session-auth.js` lost the in-window sign-in remedy and kept the HOLD; `session-reopen.js` collapsed onto `agent-window.js`; `session-dispatch.js` went from five routes to one; `session-engine.js` lost the window factory, the consent reflow and the consent-card posture source; `session-summary.js` lost `keptWindow`
  - **THE GUARDS OUTLIVE THE MACHINERY BY ONE WAVE, deliberately** — `settings.getWindowMode()` / `getPreConsentWindow()` still answer hard-OFF for every stored value, so nothing can re-arm in the gap, and they go in the next wave after a full green. `test/pre-consent-window-default.test.mjs` is that record
- ⚠ **TWO DEFECTS THE WAVE ITSELF CREATED, BOTH CAUGHT BY THE REWRITTEN TESTS AND FIXED IN IT.** They are recorded because both were SILENT: (a) `session-reopen.js › bind` REBUILDS its `deps` from a literal, so dropping `openAgentWindow` from that list discarded the handle the engine passes and `reopenByTask` then hit its own fail-closed guard on every live session — the Agents tab's "Open window" refusing in production, wearing exactly the face of a legitimately unopenable session. `bind`'s docblock now states the rebuild rule. (b) `launch()` kept a reference to `adoptable` after the `sessionConsent.has(key)` that declared it was removed — a `ReferenceError` on every call, on a branch made unreachable by an earlier early return, which is why nothing caught it until a test drove the function
- **The ~70 test files were rewritten DOWN, never deleted wholesale (§14's mixed-file rule), and that rule paid for itself repeatedly** — `session-open-thread.test.mjs` turned out to be the ONLY cover anywhere for `channel-context`'s access rules; `session-outbound-card.test.mjs` was the only pin on `RESHOW_TYPES`; `session-permission-hardening.test.mjs`'s F9 case names "the card" in its title and drives live `session-post-surface.js` in its body. Each would have gone if the title had been trusted over the assertions. 34 files were deleted outright, 34 rewritten down, the rest untouched
- Status: **RESOLVED** — the desktop suite is green at 1904 tests. The residue is F-234 (the ENDED pill has nothing to retain) and F-235 (`inboundNotice`'s orphaned copy)

- **The code does not do that.** `components/channels-v2/channels-v2-core.tsx` calls `useAgentsPanel(...)` unconditionally at page level; the `infoOpen` condition gates only the RENDERING of `ChannelsV2InfoPanel`, not the hook. (TanStack's default `refetchIntervalInBackground: false` still pauses it for a hidden browser tab, which is why nobody noticed)

Tab-scoping the hook is a real behaviour change (the tab-row badge counts peer rows, so scoping the poll to the open tab would leave the badge stale); deleting the sentence concedes a poll nobody asked for. Both sides' evidence is left in place

## F-231 — should `bypass` cover the operator's own connected MCP servers? (2026-08-20, RAISED TO SAMUEL)

- Found during: root-causing Samuel's live-test complaint that "Tools = Bypass is not honoured". Two links were broken and both were FIXED in that wave (`sessions:launch` hard-pinned `tools: 'manual'`, and the Settings tab wrote a single-use arm — INVARIANTS §11). **This entry is the part that was deliberately NOT changed**
- **The open question.** `main/session-profiles.js › BYPASS_TOOLS` is a POSITIVE allow-list — the module says so in terms (*"Unknown therefore GATES IN EVERY MODE, `bypass` included"*), and that is a deliberate containment property: a negative list auto-allows every unrecognized name, including a delegation or exfil built-in a future CLI ships. The consequence is that under the `full` profile, where the operator's OWN connected MCP servers load (no `--strict-mcp-config`), **every tool from those servers still gates under `bypass`** — and in a windowless session a gate is a deny
- **Samuel's ruling, 2026-08-20: DO NOT WIDEN THE LIST.** The wave shipped the reporting fix instead — `session-windowless.js › notifyDenied` now names the denied tool and channel in a local notification, so the failure is legible rather than silent
- ⚠ **What makes this worth an id: the operator's mental model of the word "bypass" and the list's actual reach disagree, and the notification makes that disagreement VISIBLE rather than resolving it.** Expect the question back the first time someone with a busy MCP setup runs a windowless agent. Candidate answers if it is revisited: (a) leave it, and let the notice teach the boundary; (b) admit MCP tools from servers the operator configured themselves, on the argument that configuring a server IS the grant; (c) a per-server opt-in beside the tool profile. **(b) is the one that needs the most care** — the tool profile is the containment control, and a posture that reaches past it inverts the two axes
- Status: open (product decision — do not close by widening a positive allow-list to fix a reporting gap)

## F-232 — a deferred realtime doorbell is lost if its surface unmounts mid-write (2026-08-20)

- Found during: the liveness wave, tracing why new threads sometimes need a reload
- `src/shared/realtime/refetch-coordinator.ts` correctly DEFERS (never drops) a doorbell that arrives while a local write is in flight, and `use-api-mutation.ts › useRefetchGate` releases it on both success and failure. **But the coordinator lives in a ref on the component that armed it**, so a doorbell deferred while a write is in flight, on a surface that then unmounts before the write settles, is never run and nothing re-arms it
- **Reachable in one gesture:** send a message, then navigate away from the channel before the mutation settles, while a peer posts. The reconnect catch-up covers the SOCKET case only (`shared/realtime/shared-channel-registry.ts`, and `dopl-desktop-app/main/ui-sync-core.js › catchUpBatch` on the desktop side) — this is not a socket gap, so neither one sees it
- ⚠ Low severity by frequency and self-healing on the next doorbell for that surface, which is why it is filed rather than fixed in a wave that already touched this file's neighbours. It is recorded because "the transcript quietly stopped updating" has no error shape, and this is one of the two remaining ways to produce it
- **The fix, when taken:** either hoist the coordinator above the mounting component (page-level, keyed by workspace), or flush pending deferrals on teardown. Measure first — a teardown flush on an unmounting surface may fire a refetch nothing will render
- Status: open

## ✅ F-233 — the launch panel's inbound arm is unreachable, and two INVARIANTS bullets name it as the arm's web surface (2026-08-20) — RESOLVED 2026-08-20

- Found during: the F-228 deletion wave, censusing what still consumes `src/features/channels/components/launch-panel.tsx`
- **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED.** `launch-panel.tsx` gates its disclosure on `disclosable = isInbound && hasSettings`, and `isInbound` is `request.kind === "inbound"`. The panel has exactly ONE production consumer — `components/channels-v2/thread-consent.tsx › ThreadSendBox` — which always passes an OUTBOUND request (`view-model-requested.ts › pendingOutboundByThread` filters `r.kind === "outbound"`). What DOES paint is only the outbound send box: Sparkles, "Your agent wants to reply", "To send", Send, Cancel

A third copy of the same claim sits in `components/channels-v2/settings-agent.tsx`'s docblock ("It still renders on the request card")
- **Where an inbound decision REALLY renders**, and why this went unnoticed: `thread-consent.tsx › ThreadAwaitingStrip`, `channels-v2/transcript.tsx › ThreadCardMessage` and the Inbox pane's `InboxRow` each hand-roll their own Launch agent / Decline buttons. - ⚠ **FILED, NOT FIXED, per CLAUDE.md's precedence rule** — because the two available fixes were opposite product decisions and neither was a cleanup: (a) the arm is genuinely dead, so delete it and its store key; (b) the arm is intended and its surface regressed, so re-mount `RequestPermissionRow` on the inbound surfaces that do render
- **✅ SAMUEL RULED (a), 2026-08-20, AND IT IS EXECUTED.** Deleted: `channelPermissionPresets` and its whole family in `main/channel-prefs.js` (`ARM_TTL_MS`, `armIsLive`, `resolveArm`, `readArmFrom`, `armInto`, `takeArmFrom`, `sweepExpired`, `getAllPresets`, `writeAll`, and the four public arm fns), the two `channels.*PermissionPreset` preload ops and their `channel-dir-ipc.js` handlers, the consumption in `trigger.js › inboundApproved`, both `clearPermissionPreset` teardowns in `trigger-outcomes.js`, `hooks/use-channel-permission-preset.ts`, `components/request-folder-row.tsx`, `permission-preset-row.tsx › RequestPermissionRow`, and `launch-panel.tsx`'s entire inbound half

One record remains (`channelLaunchPosture`), read at one call site (`sessions:launch`). **An inbound request now carries no tool posture at all** and starts at `manual` — strictly more restrictive than before
