- Status: **RESOLVED**

## ✅ F-234 — the ENDED-agent pill can never be retained, because retention gates on a window (2026-08-20) — RESOLVED 2026-08-20

- Found during: the F-228 deletion wave, rewriting `test/session-summary.test.mjs`'s §4 retention block
- `main/session-summary.js › noteEnded` retains an ended session's pill on `keepWindow === true && windowAlive(s && s.win)`. **Every session is windowless since 2026-08-20**, so `s.win` is null on every one of them, `windowAlive` answers false, and `endedKept` never gains a row — whatever `session-effects`' M2b passes for an abandonment. `session-engine.js › settle`'s `s.win.destroy()` is dead for the same reason
- **The consequence is a surface, not an internal:** an agent that ends leaves the Agents tab immediately instead of holding its pill, so an operator who was not watching has no record that it ran. The retention rule exists precisely for "an end nobody watched happen must not make a transcript vanish"
- ⚠ **INVARIANTS §11 states the retention as live** ("an ended session's pill outlives its registry entry (the retention rule)"), and `session-reopen.js › controlByTask` reasons from it ("SETTLED AND RETAINED-ENDED SESSIONS ANSWER `{ok:false}`"). So this is a code-vs-INVARIANTS disagreement, filed rather than fixed
- **It PREDATES the deletion wave** — it has been true since the windowless executor shipped earlier the same day — and the wave surfaced it rather than causing it. The retention machinery is intact as a FUNCTION (`noteEnded`, `sweepEnded`, `MAX_ENDED`, the LRU drop) and is kept under test with a fake window (§14) rather than deleted
- **The fix, when taken:** decide what "retain" means with no window to be alive. The obvious replacement is a time bound (retain for N minutes after settle, swept on the next projection) or an unconditional `keepWindow` honour with `MAX_ENDED` as the only bound — but the second re-opens the question the window check was answering, which is "did anything ever have this on screen". Measure what the Agents tab actually needs before picking
- **✅ SAMUEL RULED THE SECOND OPTION, 2026-08-20, AND IT IS EXECUTED.** Retention is unconditional on the caller's flag, bounded by `MAX_ENDED` alone. **The time bound was refused for the reason the entry itself gave**: the question the window check answered has no answer without a window, and a TTL would have invented one — it would have looked like a measurement of attention while measuring nothing but elapsed time. A count bound is honest about being a count
- **What went with it, because all of it was the same dead fact:** the `windowAlive` filter in `sweepEnded` (it ran on EVERY projection, so a retained row could vanish between two reads), the `win` handle carried on each retained entry, and `session-engine.js › settle`'s `if (!keepWindow && s.win && …) s.win.destroy()`. The flag now means exactly one thing — retain the ended pill
- ⚠ **THE ARGUMENT'S NAME IS STILL `keepWindow` AND WAS LEFT ALONE, deliberately.** It is the ENGINE's word, set at `session-effects.js › endEffects`; renaming it at the consumer only would leave the two sides of one flag spelled differently. Rename it at the producer or not at all
- ⚠ **THE ACCEPTED COST IS PINNED, NOT ASSUMED: a retained pill is a TOMBSTONE, not a HANDLE.** `reopenByTask` refuses a settled key, so clicking one opens nothing. That is the honest version of what the window rule was avoiding (a click that minted a fresh shell wearing a dead session's name), and `session-summary-retention.test.mjs` asserts the absence of the `keptWindow` lookup so it cannot be revived on the strength of retention working again
- ⚠ **ONE CLAIM IN THIS ENTRY WAS ITSELF WRONG, and it is corrected rather than quietly dropped.** It said "INVARIANTS §11 states the retention as live". §11 did not: the sentence quoted (*"an ended session's pill outlives its registry entry (the retention rule)"*) is `session-reopen.js › controlByTask`'s docblock, a SOURCE comment. §11 carried no retention bullet at all, which is arguably worse — the rule was live, broken, and undocumented. It has one now
- **Tests:** §4 of `session-summary.test.mjs` moved out whole to `session-summary-retention.test.mjs` (that file was at EXACTLY 500 — F-226). ⚠ **No fake window survives in it.** The old cases drove the predicate through `fakeWindow()` *because the source was live while the engine could no longer reach it*, which is precisely how a suite stays green over a rule production cannot run; the regression case now drives `win: null` directly. Two tests elsewhere were rewritten to the rule that survives rather than deleted — `session-crash-teardown`'s destroy assertion, which had said in terms "it goes when the line goes, in the same change", and `session-summary-report`'s third beat, whose subject was an operator closing a window
- Status: **RESOLVED**

## ✅ F-236 — the windowless message-axis floor was LAUNCH-ONLY, and a held reply had nothing to release it (2026-08-20) — RESOLVED 2026-08-20

- Found during: the read-only audit of `dopl-desktop-app/` that F-234 and F-235 were verified in — sweeping for "two code paths answering one question". This is the one that turned out to be a live defect rather than debt
- **THE DEFECT, reachable in ONE gesture from the shipped UI.** A windowless session has NO ACCEPT SURFACE. `session-gate.js › enqueue` HOLDS an inbound reply whenever `autoInbound(s)` is false, and the whole family that released one — `decideInbound`, `drainQueue`, `drainInbound` — was deleted with the session window (F-228), **on the stated grounds that "a windowless session's message axis is FLOORED at `auto_inbound`, so the queue never holds"**
- ⚠ **THAT WAS TRUE OF THE LAUNCH LANES AND OF NOTHING ELSE.** `channel-prefs.js › windowlessMessageMode` floors both spawn paths. Nothing floored a mode set on a session ALREADY RUNNING: `session-reopen.js › setModeByTask` accepted all four values, `session-reducer.js` coerced against the full table, and `agent-posture.tsx` renders `MESSAGE_OPTIONS` — which includes `"ask"` — on every live agent
- **THE CONSEQUENCE, traced end to end.** Pick "Ask each time" → `autoInbound` false → `enqueue` gates → `session-io.js › queueInbound(…, true)` holds. The head emits `inbound_pending`, which `session-windowless.js › claimGate` does NOT claim (it handles `outbound_gate` and `permission_request` only) and `session-engine.js › emit` drops on the null `win`. The accept events have no caller. **The session parks at `awaiting_inbound` forever, `io.noteGatedBody` records the body, and session-seed and session-history both filter it out — so the peer's message is invisible to the agent permanently, with no error anywhere.** That is the AUDIT D2 failure `session-gate.js` was written to prevent, reached from the far end
- **WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE.** Every gate here was green: the launch lanes really do floor, the reducer really does coerce fail-closed, the axes suite really does pin the truth tables. **The missing thing was not a check on a value — it was a check that the two WRITERS of one field agreed**, and there was no test that named both lanes in one place. The audit found it by asking who writes `messageMode`, not by asking whether any writer was wrong
- **THE FIX (Samuel's ruling: floor the live axis).** `session-profiles.js › floorWindowlessMessage` is the ONE statement of the rule; `setModeByTask` applies it when the resolved session is windowless. It lives at that layer and not at the IPC boundary **because only that layer has resolved the SESSION and can see whether it has a surface**
  - **It CLAMPS, it does not refuse.** An operator asking for `auto_outbound` wanted less supervision on the OUT half and gets exactly that; a refusal would leave the select showing a value main is not enforcing, which is the lie that surface has been fixed for twice. The reply is main's post-dispatch truth, so the UI renders the floored value
  - **It widens SUPERVISION, never CONTAINMENT** — `grantDecision` returns off Axis B before Axis A is consulted, and the profile is checked first
  - **It is keyed on `windowless`, not written unconditionally.** The floor is a fact about having no Accept surface; nothing in this tree currently mints a windowed session, but hard-coding today's shape into a rule about a CAPABILITY is how the original bug was written
- **`test/session-mode-floor.test.mjs` pins the rule as a PROPERTY, not a table** — every message mode must floor to one `autoInbound` accepts, so a fifth mode fails there rather than silently reintroducing the hold — pins both lanes against each other mode for mode, and pins the unreleasability as an ABSENCE so whoever builds an accept surface reads it first
- ⚠ **THE SPA HALF IS NOT DONE AND IS DELIBERATELY OUT OF THIS CHANGE.** `agent-posture.tsx` still offers "Ask each time" on a live agent; main now clamps it, so the failure is a select that snaps back rather than a lost message. **Dropping the option from the live selector is the SPA fixer's** — this change did not touch `src/`
- **The same sweep found a THIRD unpinned copy of the mode tables** (`channel-prefs.js`'s WRITE validator, asserted against literals and never against `session-profiles`), which REJECTS a value outside its lists — so a fifth canonical mode would have made the durable posture silently unwritable with every suite green. Cross-pinned in the axes suite, with the SPA's fourth copy stated rather than asserted
- Status: **RESOLVED** (main-process half; the SPA selector is a separate change)

## ✅ F-235 — `session-gate.js › inboundNotice` survives with no caller and copy naming a deleted surface (2026-08-20) — RESOLVED 2026-08-20

- Found during: the F-228 deletion wave, after `notifyInbound` / `surface` / `windowHasFocus` were removed from `main/session-gate.js`
- `inboundNotice(item)` built the banner the gate raised for a HELD inbound reply. The banner is gone; the builder is not. `grep -rn inboundNotice main/` returns only its own definition and its export — **zero callers** (`trigger.js` sends `consent.notifyInbound` and its own mention banner, neither of which is this)
- ⚠ **ITS FALLBACK BODY IS `"Open the session window to accept or decline it."`** — a sentence naming a surface that does not exist and an action with no control behind it. That is worse than a dead function: it is dead COPY, and copy is what a future wiring reuses without re-reading
- **Kept rather than deleted, and the reason is not sentiment:** a windowless session that needs to tell the operator something about an inbound turn is a real gap (the message axis is floored at `auto_inbound`, so nothing holds *today*, but the floor is a posture decision and not a law), and this function is the only surviving statement of what that copy should look like — one line, bounded, calm fallbacks, no em dash. `test/inbound-gate-notify.test.mjs` pins the string as-shipped plus a CENSUS case that goes red the moment a caller appears, so whoever wires one must re-read the copy first
- **The fix, when taken:** either rewrite the body for a surface that exists and wire it, or delete the function and its test together. **Do not wire it as it stands.**
- **✅ SAMUEL RULED DELETE, 2026-08-20, AND IT IS EXECUTED** — function, export, copy and the two test cases that drove it, together
- **THE ARGUMENT FOR KEEPING IT WAS ANSWERED, NOT OVERRULED.** The entry kept it because "a windowless session that DOES need to tell the operator something about an inbound turn is a real gap", and noted the message axis was floored at `auto_inbound` so nothing holds *today* — *"but the floor is a posture decision and not a law"*. **That was the right worry and it was worse than the entry knew: the floor did not hold.** It was applied at LAUNCH only, and a mode set on a RUNNING session went straight past it (F-236, found in the same sweep and fixed first). With the floor now applied on every lane, nothing can be held on a surface-less session — so there is no turn to notify anybody about, and the copy was for a notice that is not going to be built
- ⚠ **THE STANDING CONDITION IS PINNED WHERE THE DELETION HAPPENED.** `test/inbound-gate-notify.test.mjs` asserts the floor still exists AND that the live lane applies it, so if the floor is ever lifted the file that lost the notice is the one that goes red. Whoever wants one then is writing a NEW design against a surface that exists, which is what the entry actually wanted
- **The absence is asserted in all three parts** — the function, its export, and the string *"Open the session window"* — across the whole of `main/`, so a revival cannot bring back the copy without bringing back the review
- Status: **RESOLVED**

## ✅ F-237 — a cross-tree test pinned a FILENAME, and a desktop refactor reddened the root suite (2026-08-20) — RESOLVED 2026-08-20

- Found during: the read-only audit of `src/` + `apps/` + `packages/`, at the very first suite run — it was **already red at `HEAD`**, before the audit changed anything
- **THE BREAK.** `components/channels-v2/settings-agent-posture.test.tsx` asserted H2's one-consumer rule as `desktopSource("channel-dir-ipc.js")` `.toContain("channelPrefs.launchStartModes(p.channelId)")`. The desktop split that file and the read moved to `main/session-ipc-ops.js` — **a pure move that changed nothing about the rule** — and the assertion failed
- ⚠ **THE FILENAME WAS NEVER THE INVARIANT.** H2 is enforced by there being exactly ONE reader of the stored launch posture; WHICH file holds it is the desktop's business and is expected to move. The test pinned the most volatile fact available and called it the rule
- **THE CLASS IS THE FINDING, not this one assertion.** This is a **cross-tree source-text test**: it lives in `src/`, reads `dopl-desktop-app/main/`, and is therefore INVISIBLE to the desktop's own suite. A desktop refactor can red the root suite with no signal on the side that made the change, and the desktop author has no reason to look. Every such assertion is a tripwire pointing the wrong way
- **THE FIX.** `channels-v2/settings-agent-harness.tsx › desktopMainFilesContaining` counts the files in `main/` containing a needle, so the assertion is a CONSUMER COUNT. It survives a move and still fails on what matters — a second reader appearing. Applied to this one assertion
- ⚠ **THE REST OF THE CLASS IS NOT SWEPT.** Other `desktopSource(...)` assertions in `src/` still name files (`channel-prefs.js` is the common one, and it is a stable definition site rather than a wiring site, so it is much less exposed). **Not audited file by file; the pattern to prefer is stated here rather than enforced anywhere**
- Status: **RESOLVED** (the assertion), **OPEN as a pattern** — see the sweep note above

## F-238 — the SPA's bridge mirror has no guard, and it drifted twice in one day (2026-08-20)

- Found during: the same audit, diffing `src/shared/lib/spa-bridge.ts` against `apps/desktop-ui/src/lib/dopl-bridge.ts` member by member
- **`dopl-bridge.ts`'s `channels` block was wrong in BOTH directions at once.** It declared `getPermissionPreset` / `setPermissionPreset` — ops `renderer/app-preload.js` had DELETED with the single-use arm — and omitted `getLaunchPosture` / `setLaunchPosture` / `getAutoSend` / `setAutoSend`, **all four of which the web tree actively calls** (`hooks/use-channel-launch-posture.ts`, `hooks/use-channel-auto-send.ts`)
- ⚠ **THE OMISSION IS THE DANGEROUS HALF.** The shared tree feature-detects each capability and renders **nothing** when it is absent, so a gap in the mirror does not fail — **it deletes a feature silently** (INVARIANTS §11 states exactly this about the preload; the same logic reaches the mirror). Declaring a dead op is merely noise; hiding a live one is an invisible product regression
- **WHY IT DRIFTED: the ops were added and removed on the DESKTOP side, and nothing on the web side is held against them.** `test/preload-parity.test.mjs › APP_OPS` pins the PRELOAD's inventory and fails on add as well as remove — an excellent guard, on one of the four files the surface spans. The TS mirrors have no equivalent, so the pin can be green while the mirror is two ops behind in each direction
- **The corrected mirror is committed** (2026-08-20); this entry is about the ABSENCE OF A GUARD, which is untouched
- **THE REMEDY IS NOT "ANOTHER SOURCE-TEXT TEST", and F-237 above is why.** A test in `src/` that greps `app-preload.js` is the same tripwire pointing the same wrong way. Better shapes, in order: (a) have `APP_OPS` — which already runs the preload against a fake `electron` — ALSO assert the mirror's declared members, so the one existing pin covers all the files it already claims move together; (b) generate the TS mirror from the preload; (c) accept the risk and say so here
- ⚠ **`spa-bridge.ts` and `dopl-bridge.ts` also disagree on two members that are NOT drift but read like it**: `onAuthState` is required in one and optional in the other, and `apiRequest`'s `opts` is optional in one and required in the other. Harmless today (each side types the slice it uses, which `shared/lib/desktop.ts` states as the rule) — **recorded so the next reader does not "fix" one to match the other and change a call signature**
- Status: **OPEN**

## F-239 — the agent window's ROUTE addresses a thread, and a thread now holds several agents (2026-08-21) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the SPA half of the MULTIPLAYER AGENTS wave (the "New Agent" button; `agents-model.ts › agentKey` re-keyed onto the agent's own id)
- **`sessions.launch` now mints a NEW agent per click**, so `(channelId, taskId)` identifies a THREAD and no longer identifies one agent. Every list surface was re-keyed onto `agentId` in the same change — the Agents tab draws one card per agent, marks exactly one "Viewing", and the thread Info tab lists them all by id
- ⚠ **THE AGENT WINDOW WAS NOT, AND COULD NOT BE, because its address is a ROUTE.** `components/channels-v2/agent-window.tsx` receives `channelId` + `?thread=` from `main/agent-window.js` and nothing else, so it resolves the pair against the feed and **lands on whichever of the operator's agents that thread happens to hold first**. The lookup was changed from `agentKey` to a direct pair match in the same pass — that is the honest expression of what the route can answer, not a fix
- **The same shape reaches the bridge OPS.** `main/session-summary.js`'s own 2026-08-21 header states that `pause` / `end` / `setMode` / `message` / narration / `openAgentWindow` each take the agent id as a third coordinate; `components/channels-v2/agents-controls.ts` still calls them with `(channelId, taskId)` because `shared/lib/spa-bridge.ts` — the desktop's declaration, and out of that pass's scope — had not widened yet. **Until it does, a stop verb on a shared thread is as ambiguous as the window is**
- **The remedy is one decision, not two:** carry `agentId` in the window's route (a third param, or `?agent=`), and add it to each op's signature in `spa-bridge.ts` + its `apps/desktop-ui/src/lib/dopl-bridge.ts` mirror. Both callers already hold the session object, so neither needs a parse. ⚠ **Do it in ONE change** — a widened op with a route that cannot name an agent just moves the ambiguity
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-21, in the desktop half of the same wave, and the remedy is the one written above — BOTH halves in one change.**
  - **Route:** `main/agent-window.js › agentRoute` emits `?thread=<id>&agent=<id>`, and `agentWindowKey` gained the third part, so a window is one per AGENT rather than one per thread. Both are OPTIONAL — a caller that knows only the pair still gets its old route and its old key. ⚠ **A CHANNEL-LEVEL AGENT HAS NO THREAD**, so the route now requires `thread` OR `agent` rather than `thread`, and omits the selection it does not have.
  - **Ops:** `reopen` / `openAgentWindow` / `message` / `setMode` / `narration` / `pause` / `end` each take a trailing OPTIONAL `agentId` — in `spa-bridge.ts`, in the `dopl-bridge.ts` mirror, in `renderer/app-preload.js`, and at the boundary in `main/session-ipc-ops.js` (clamped by the real `agent-id.js` charset, malformed values degraded to `''` rather than refused, on `segment`'s terms).
  - ⚠ **OPTIONAL WAS A DELIBERATE CHOICE, not a compatibility shrug.** A REQUIRED third argument breaks every existing caller at once and offers nothing a fallback cannot: an omitted id resolves to the OLDEST live agent on the thread (`main/session-reopen.js › resolveSession`), which is byte-for-byte what a caller got when a thread could hold only one session. A NAMED id resolves EXACTLY and answers nothing when it is wrong or dead — **"pause my agent" must never pause a different one**, which is the half that would have been unsafe to leave to a fallback.
  - **`session-summary.js` now EMITS the id it was already assumed to** (`agentId` beside `name`, on live and retained-ended entries alike), and `spa-bridge.ts › DesktopSessionSummary` DECLARES it, so the SPA's defensive read is a typed one.
  - **What is NOT resolved and was not in scope:** the agent-window RENDERER still has to pick its agent out of the feed. It now has `?agent=` to do it with; whether it reads that param is the SPA's call.
- ✅ **THE SPA HALF LANDED 2026-08-22** — the sentence above is answered, and the seam held: neither side had to change the other's file.
  - **Ops:** `components/channels-v2/agents-controls.ts` passes `agentId` on all six, **read off the SESSION OBJECT each surface is already showing and never re-derived from a key or a route**. Call sites: `agent-composer.tsx` (the 1:1 lane), `agent-panel-controls.tsx` (pause / end / open), `agent-posture.tsx` (setMode). `agents-multiplayer.test.tsx › the bridge ops address ONE agent` pins each, **and pins the `undefined` degradation beside it** so the fallback stays a fallback and never hardens into a refusal.
  - **Route:** `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/agent-window/index.tsx` reads `?agent=` and `components/channels-v2/agent-window.tsx` prefers it, falling back to first-on-thread when it is absent.
  - ⚠ **THE FALLBACK IS WHERE THE REMAINING RISK LIVES, and it is worth naming even on a closed finding.** Every degradation here is silent and plausible: an omitted id does not fail, it acts on the OLDEST live agent and reports success. That is correct for an older main and wrong for a new one that simply forgot to pass the id — and the two are indistinguishable at the call site. The tests are the only thing holding the difference, which is why each op has both cases rather than the happy one.
- Status: **RESOLVED** — route + ops + summary field on the desktop (2026-08-21), ops + route reader on the SPA (2026-08-22)

## F-240 — `cn()` silently drops a class whenever a custom `text-*` SIZE meets a `text-*` COLOUR (2026-08-21) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-30 (residual fixed in the same change)

- Found during: the transcript's markdown renderer, composing the body's block recipe with a heading's and a code fence's
- **MEASURED, not inferred** (2026-08-21, `tailwind-merge@^3.5.0`): `twMerge("wrap-anywhere max-w-[92%] text-lead text-text-primary", "text-body font-semibold")` returns `"wrap-anywhere max-w-[92%] text-body font-semibold"` — **the COLOUR is gone.** The same call with `"list-disc pl-5"` keeps it, so the loss depends entirely on what the second argument happens to contain
- **THE CAUSE IS THIS TREE'S TYPE SCALE, and it is not a bug in `tailwind-merge`.** The scale is `text-lead` / `text-body` / `text-small` / `text-caption` / `text-micro` / `text-label` (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md), and the colour utilities are `text-text-primary` / `text-text-muted` / `text-link` / … Both are `text-<word>`. `tailwind-merge` resolves conflict groups by class NAME against a config it ships, so a custom size scale it has never heard of is indistinguishable from a colour, and it puts them in one group where the last one wins
- ⚠ **THE FAILURE IS INVISIBLE IN REVIEW AND IN TESTS.** Nothing errors; the element inherits a colour or a size from an ancestor and usually looks *nearly* right. It only bites where the ancestor's value differs — which is exactly the case a themed surface or a nested panel creates
- **The renderer avoids it by construction rather than by merging carefully**: `message-markdown.tsx` takes the geometry and the type as TWO props and hands each block only the ones it should not have to win against (its rule 5). **That is a local fix. The general hazard is untouched** — `grep -rn 'cn(' src | grep 'text-'` is the shape of the sweep, and it has not been run
- **Remedies, in order:** (a) teach `tailwind-merge` the scale via `extendTailwindMerge({ classGroups: { 'font-size': [{ text: ['lead','body','small','caption','micro','label','stat'] }] } })` in `shared/lib/utils.ts` — one edit, fixes every call site at once, and is the reason that wrapper exists; (b) rename the colour utilities out of the `text-*` namespace (large, breaks every component); (c) accept it and keep splitting recipes by hand, which is what today's code does
- ⚠ **(a) MUST BE MEASURED BEFORE IT IS TRUSTED.** Widening the group changes what `cn` drops at every existing call site in the tree, and some of them may be relying on today's behaviour without knowing it
- Status: **OPEN**
- ⚠ **CLOSED 2026-08-30 — superseded SIX WEEKS BEFORE IT WAS FILED.** Remedy (a) had already shipped: `src/shared/lib/utils.ts › twMerge` is `extendTailwindMerge` with a `font-size` classGroup, landed 2026-07-07 (`e9c6d6cc`, found with `git log -S 'extendTailwindMerge'`) against this entry's 2026-08-21 filing. ⚠ **An entry that is superseded before it is written is a REVIEW failure, not a code one** — the check was one `git log -S` away.
- 🔴 **RESIDUAL, KEPT: `text-stat` is the one type-ramp rung MISSING from that `font-size` classGroup**, which lists eight (`micro, label, caption, small, body, lead, title, display`) while `--text-stat: 26px` is a real rung in BOTH `src/app/globals.css` and `apps/desktop-ui/src/styles/tokens.css`. So any `cn()` composing `text-stat` with a `text-*` colour still drops one silently — **live at `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/overview/overview-bits.tsx › StatFigure`**, which pairs `text-stat` with `text-text-primary` in one `className` and imports `cn` from that same module.
- ✅ **THE RESIDUAL IS FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE (2026-08-30): `stat` is in the classGroup**, and the docblock above it now says the list IS the type ramp, so a rung added to the ramp is a rung added there. **The whole entry is closed.**

## F-241 — a PEER's desktop keeps pushing a session for a thread that was just deleted, and the FK makes the whole push 500 (2026-08-21)

- Found during: shipping THREAD DELETION (`channels/server/service-tasks-delete.ts › deleteTask`; INVARIANTS §5)
- **The shape.** `channel_sessions.task_id REFERENCES channel_tasks(id)` (`20260805120000`). The deleting operator's own agents are ended client-side first (`components/channels-v2/thread-manage.tsx`), but **a PEER's agent is not reachable from any server** — it lives in another main process and stops on its own idle/abandon timer (accepted, Samuel 2026-08-21). Until it does, that desktop keeps reporting the session, and `channels/server/session-state-service.ts › toUpsert` sets `task_id: entry.threadId ?? null` — **an id that no longer has a row**
- **The consequence is wider than the one session.** `repository-sessions.ts › replaceSessionStates` upserts the whole changed set in ONE statement and rethrows any error, so a single `23503` fails the entire `reportSessionStates` call — **that operator's every OTHER session stops being reported too**, and their peer cards go stale workspace-wide until the dead agent times out. `POST` answers 500; the desktop logs it and retries on the next state change, so it is self-healing but noisy and mis-attributed
- ⚠ **NOT CAUSED BY THE CASCADE'S SESSION STEP, and removing that step does not fix it.** With the step gone the FK's `ON DELETE SET NULL` would null the stored row's `task_id`, but the peer's next push still REPORTS the dead id and still violates the constraint on the way in. The hazard is inherent to a thread being deletable while a peer holds it
- **MEASURED?** No — this is read from the schema and the two functions above, not from a reproduction. **Reproduce before fixing**: run an agent on a thread from a second account, delete the thread from the first, and watch the second machine's next session push
- **Remedies, in order.** (a) `toUpsert` / `replaceSessionStates` degrade a `23503` on `task_id` to `task_id: null` and keep the rest of the set — smallest, keeps the row's honest half (a live agent with no thread), and is the shape `listSessionStates`' narrow `PGRST205` degrade already models; (b) the desktop drops a session whose thread 404s on read — correct but needs a desktop release and a floor raise (§13); (c) accept, and make the failure quiet rather than a 500. ⚠ **Do NOT widen `replaceSessionStates` into a blanket try/catch** — a swallowed write here reports a store that did not happen, which its own docblock refuses for exactly this reason
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-21 by remedy (a), server-side only** — `repository-sessions.ts › healDeadThreadRefs`, reached from `replaceSessionStates`'s upsert. On a `23503` it re-reads which of the REPORTED thread ids still have a `channel_tasks` row, nulls `task_id` on **only the dead ones**, and retries the upsert ONCE. Nothing else in the set is touched, and a live row keeps its thread
  - **WHY NULLING IS HONEST RATHER THAN A SWALLOW:** the row's other half — *user U is running an agent, in channel C, state working* — is still true, and a null `task_id` is exactly what the column's own `ON DELETE SET NULL` would have left had the row been stored a moment earlier. Dropping the row instead would lose a LIVE agent from the projection; nulling the whole batch would discard the thread of rows whose threads are fine
  - ⚠ **IT NEVER GUESSES WHICH CONSTRAINT FAILED.** `channel_sessions` has four FKs and the match is on the CODE alone (the house rule — a constraint name in an error message is prose). If nothing in the batch names a dead thread the ORIGINAL error is rethrown: a `23503` on `channel_id` means the CHANNEL is gone, which nulling a thread id cannot fix and must not be made to look fixed
  - ⚠ **ONE RETRY, BY CONSTRUCTION** — the healer returns rows, the caller upserts once more and throws. No loop, so a violation this degrade does not cover cannot spin. The existence probe runs on the FAILURE PATH ONLY; a pre-flight check on every push would add a query per push to protect against a once-per-deleted-thread race, which is the cost this table's design refuses
  - **Pinned by `repository-sessions-replace.test.ts › "replaceSessionStates — a thread deleted under a live peer agent (F-241)"`** (⚠ it lived in `repository-sessions.test.ts` until 2026-09-01, when the health columns split that file at the §1 cap; the anchor moved with the test) — five cases: the replace SUCCEEDS with one dead `task_id` and only that row nulled; a `23503` naming no dead thread rethrows; a report with no thread ids never probes; every other write error still surfaces; a second failure throws rather than looping
  - **Remedy (b) is still worth doing later and is not blocked by this** — a desktop that drops a session whose thread 404s stops reporting the dead id at all. This makes the server survive it; that would stop it happening
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-21, remedy (a))

## F-250 — the agent window's Work lane was FROZEN on every build: it filtered live frames on a two-segment key main stopped sending (2026-08-21) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: an adversarial read of the channels-v2 agent surfaces after the multiplayer-agents wave
- **The shape.** `components/channels-v2/use-agent-narration.ts` built `${channelId}:${taskId}` and dropped every pushed frame whose `sessionKey` did not equal it. Main sends `s.key` (`dopl-desktop-app/main/session-narration.js › flush`), and that key is `main/session-store.js › sessionKey` — **`<channelId>:<taskId>:<agentId>`, three segments since multiplayer.** The compare could therefore never match on ANY build, single-agent included
- ⚠ **THERE IS NO ERROR SHAPE, WHICH IS WHY IT SHIPPED.** The window renders; the header, the meter and the posture strip all run off the SUMMARIES feed and stay live; only the lane the window exists for stops. After the one mount read it never moved again
- **AND THE MOUNT READ WAS ALSO WRONG.** `sessions.narration(channelId, taskId)` passed no `agentId`, and main resolves that call against its blended slot (`session-store.js › slotKey`), so the first paint showed the thread's OLDEST live agent's ring under a header naming a different one
- ⚠ **THE TEST SUITE COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT.** `agent-window.test.tsx` stubbed `onNarration` as a bare unsubscriber, so **no case in the file ever drove a frame**: every narration assertion read the mount value, and the live half had zero coverage
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-22.** `useAgentNarration(channelId, taskId, agentId?)` — the read passes the id through, and the filter is `narrationMatches`: an EXACT compare on `<channel>:<thread>:<agent>` when the id is known, and the `<channel>:<thread>:` PREFIX when it is not. `agent-window.tsx` passes the RESOLVED summary's `agent?.agentId`, not the route's `?agent=` param, since main does not emit that param yet
  - **The absent-id fallback is the honest degradation, not a refusal.** A main that emits no `agentId` on its summaries also runs at most one agent per thread, so the prefix names exactly that agent; a dead lane would be strictly worse. ⚠ The prefix's **trailing colon is load-bearing**, the same way `session-store.js › threadKeyPrefix` says it is
  - ⚠ **THE RING IS NOW HELD UNDER THE KEY IT WAS ASKED FOR** (`NarrationFrame`), not as a bare array. The window resolves its agent asynchronously, so the hook mounts with no id and gains one a tick later — a bare array plus the existing `prev ??` guard would have KEPT the first (id-less) answer and discarded the exact read that followed, which is the same frozen lane by another route. Storing the key beside the ring makes a stale answer simply not match, with no `setState` in an effect to reset it (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` is an ERROR in this tree)
  - **No bridge change was needed** — `src/shared/lib/spa-bridge.ts`, `apps/desktop-ui/src/lib/dopl-bridge.ts` and `dopl-desktop-app/renderer/app-preload.js` already declared and forwarded the optional third argument. Only the SPA reader had not been updated
  - **Pinned by five new cases** in `agent-window.test.tsx › "the work lane follows the live push"`, over a bridge fake that now CAPTURES `onNarration` subscribers and fans frames out as main does: the agent's own frame lands, a sibling's is ignored, the id-less build still follows the prefix, another thread's frame is ignored (`t-1` must not match `t-12`), and the mount read names the instance. Verified to FAIL against the old two-segment key
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

## F-251 — with N of my agents on one thread, every agent's Sent lane showed every sibling's posts (2026-08-21) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the same adversarial read as F-250
- **The shape.** `components/channels-v2/agent-panel.tsx › agentSentMessages` matched on `taskId` + `authorKind: "agent"` + the viewer's own account. All three are correct and all three **stop at the THREAD.** Multiplayer puts N of ONE operator's agents on one thread, and every one of them posts under that one account with `authorKind: "agent"` — so each agent's panel and each agent's window attributed all of their siblings' words to the agent on screen. The surface whose entire promise is "this ONE agent, from the inside"
- **The discriminator already existed.** `dopl-desktop-app/main/session-outbound-tag.js › nextOwnPostId` stamps every post `agent-<agentId>-<n>` into `client_msg_id`, which the read DTO returns as `ChannelMessage.clientMsgId`; `main/session-dispatch.js › wroteIt` already uses it to keep an agent out of its own fan-out. Nothing else on the wire can tell two of one operator's agents apart
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-22.** `agentSentMessages(messages, taskId, currentUserId, agentId?)`, applied at both consumers — the panel's `SentFeed` (`agent.agentId`) and the window's WorkStream Sent lane (`agent?.agentId`, the same helper, still imported rather than re-written)
  - ⚠ **THE SUGGESTED FIX WAS `clientMsgId?.startsWith("agent-<id>-")` AND THAT WAS WRONG TWICE; the shipped rule EXCLUDES ONLY WHAT IS POSITIVELY ATTRIBUTED TO SOMEBODY ELSE.** (1) Requiring the stamp would have HIDDEN three real classes of row — a main older than the stamp, an agent that supplied its own `client_msg_id` (an idempotency decision `session-outbound-tag.js` deliberately never overwrites), and every courtesy no-op `main/channel-post.js › postResult` sends, which is a statement about the MACHINE and carries `agent-<channelId>-<seq>`. Trading one wrong lane for a silently short one is a worse deal: a lane that omits an agent's words is the harder failure to notice. (2) A `startsWith` over a loose id class **also mis-attributes that channel-scoped stamp**, because a channel UUID can begin with eight characters matching the agent-id charset (`main/agent-id.js › AGENT_ID_RE`). The shipped matcher is `/^agent-([a-z][a-z0-9]{7})-\d+$/`, **anchored at both ends** — the UUID form's four extra `-` groups are what make that decisive
  - **No `agentId` at all falls back byte for byte:** such a main runs one agent per thread, so the thread IS the instance
  - **Pinned by `agent-sent-messages.test.ts › "and WHICH of my agents posted it"` (its own file since this change — `agents-tab.test.tsx` reached the 500-line cap, and the render-vs-pure seam is where it split)** — two siblings each seeing only their own; the id-less fallback (and a whitespace-only id); and an unstamped row plus a deliberately id-shaped channel-scoped stamp both surviving the filter
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

The `MAX_SESSION_WINDOWS` paragraph is kept — it is a second dead reference this docblock has already survived once

## F-257 — `startResume` was the one spawn outside the funnel, and it resumed pre-multiplayer records with `agentId: null` (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: an adversarially-verified review of the multiplayer + ended-agent waves, censusing every caller of `session-engine.js › startSession`
- **THE SHAPE.** `session-launch.js › launch` is the SPAWN FUNNEL and mints the instance id there precisely "so no session can exist without an address". `session-park.js › startResume` — the opt-in resume behind the startup interrupted-notice — builds its own spec and does not go through it. It passed `rec.agentId || null` straight through
- ⚠ **AND `rec.agentId` IS ABSENT ON EVERY RECORD WRITTEN BEFORE 2026-08-21**, which is every record on a shipped operator's disk at the time of the wave. Those are exactly the records a crash resume reads
- **WHAT `null` COST, AND IT IS NOT LOCAL.** `session-summary.js › nameOf` answers `''` for a session with no id (deliberately — inventing a name there would be worse) → `session-state-push.js › reportRow` files `name: ""` → the server's `schema-sessions.ts › SESSION_NAME_RE` refuses it → **zod validates the ARRAY, so ONE such row 400s the WHOLE payload**. `retryable(400)` is false, `pushedDigest` is never recorded, and **every later push for that workspace fails identically for the life of the run** — `read_sessions` answers `[]` for the machine, live sessions included, and stale rows are never cleared. Same wedge `serverReportable` (C-2) and `liveForWire` were written for, reached by a third road
- **RESOLVED — both halves.** (a) `startResume` mints: `isAgentId(rec.agentId) ? rec.agentId : newAgentId()`, used for the slot key AND the spec. ⚠ It also writes the mint back onto the record, because `offerResume` holds that object in its notification click handler and the mint would otherwise defeat the check-then-act guard for exactly the legacy records it exists for — a second click would start a second session on one `sdkSessionId`. (b) BELT: `session-state-push.js › nameReportable` restates `channel_sessions.name`'s CHECK and drops any row that fails it, with one diag line per session, so no future producer can wedge a workspace
- **Tests:** five new cases in `test/session-park.test.mjs` (mint / keep / re-mint a malformed id / the write-back / the counter), three in `test/session-state-push.test.mjs` (the drop, the predicate table, the diag). ⚠ The three session-park harnesses now inject the REAL `main/agent-id.js` and a fake `slotKey` of the REAL three-part shape — the old fake mirrored the DELETED D2 choice (`agentId` OR `taskId`), so a case could pass against a key production never builds
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

## F-258 — a crash resume re-minted `client_msg_id`s the server already had, and its replies were silently discarded (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the same review, reading `session-outbound-tag.js › nextOwnPostId` against what a resume actually rehydrates
- **THE SHAPE, and it is a two-fact bug.** The per-instance post stamp is `agent-<agentId>-<n>`. Fact one: `agentId` is PERSISTED and deliberately re-used by `startResume` ("a resumed session keeps its AGENT INSTANCE ID, else it comes back as a stranger"). Fact two: `n` counts from `s.ownPostSeq`, which `session-engine.js › startSession` initialised to **0 on every session object**. Either alone is fine; together they mean a crash+resume re-mints `agent-<id>-1, 2, 3…`
- ⚠ **THE SYMPTOM IS SILENCE, ON BOTH SIDES.** Those ids already have rows, so the server's idempotency short-circuit answers the OLD row and writes nothing. The resumed agent gets `{ok}` with a stale message id and believes it replied; the peer waiting on the thread gets nothing; no error is raised anywhere and the transcript does not say a message was suppressed
- **RESOLVED.** The counter is whitelisted onto the durable record (`session-io.js › baseRecord`, `session-store.js › durableSessionRecord`, coerced harder than its sibling counters because it is CONCATENATED into an id rather than compared against a cap) and rehydrated through `session-store.js › resumedPostSeq`. ⚠ **WITH SLACK (`RESUME_POST_SEQ_SLACK`, 50), which is not belt-and-braces but the actual requirement:** the record is written at spawn / system-init / park / settle, so it always lags the posts a crash hid, and resuming from a lower bound IS the collision. Slack is free — `n` is scoped to one random instance id, nothing reads it as a count, and `MAX_OWN_POST_IDS` bounds the lookback regardless
- **Tests:** three cases in `test/session-outbound-tag.test.mjs`, one of which reconstructs the whole incident (post, persist, post, post, crash, resume) and asserts no collision; the rehydrate line is lifted out of the shipping `startSession` by regex so the case cannot pass against a number the test made up
- ⚠ **THE SERVER HALF OF THE SAME SENTENCE IS A DIFFERENT BUG** and is F-259
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

## F-259 — SECURITY: message idempotency was CHANNEL-scoped, so any member could pre-claim another operator's agent's keys and swallow its posts (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the same review, following `client_msg_id` from the desktop stamp to the write
- **THE VULNERABILITY.** `service-writes.ts › postMessage`'s short-circuit read `repository-messages.ts › findMessageByClientId(channel.id, key)` — scoped to the CHANNEL — and the unique index behind it was `(channel_id, client_msg_id)`. So "I already sent this, give me back what you stored" was a contract with the whole ROOM rather than with the retrying author
- ⚠ **THE KEYS ARE NEITHER SECRET NOR RANDOM ON THE CALLER THAT SETS THEM AT SCALE.** The desktop stamps `agent-<agentId>-<n>` (`session-outbound-tag.js › nextOwnPostId`); `agentId` is published to every workspace member as `channel_sessions.name` via `read_sessions`; `n` counts from 1. **The next several keys of every visible agent are guessable.** A member posts messages carrying them; when the victim agent posts, the server finds the pre-claimed row, writes nothing, and answers `{ok}` with the attacker's message id. Agent believes it replied, peer gets silence, no error either side
- **RESOLVED — and it took BOTH halves, which is the part the first read of this finding got wrong.** Author-scoping only the query converts the silent swallow into a `23505` the caller sees as a 500: the probe misses, the INSERT still hits a channel-scoped index, and the race repair (also author-scoped) finds nothing and rethrows. So: (a) a NEW `repository-messages.ts › findOwnMessageByClientId` narrows on `(channel_id, client_msg_id, author_user_id)` and is `postMessage`'s only probe, in both the short-circuit and the lost-race repair; (b) `supabase/migrations/20260822120000_channel_messages_author_scoped_idempotency.sql` widens the unique index to match
- ⚠ **`findMessageByClientId` SURVIVED AS THE CHANNEL-SCOPED READ, AND IS DELETED (2026-09-02).** It was kept for `storedOpeningSeq`, which asked the CROSS-AUTHOR question by design: a create that converged on somebody else's thread posted nothing and READ the winner's opening seq. **That whole arm went when `channel_tasks` took the same author scope** (`20260913120000`, `repository-tasks.ts › findOwnTaskByClientId`) — a colliding key from another member now yields a SEPARATE thread instead of converging, so nothing reads across authors and an orphan repository helper would read as a live door. The sentence below about column order is therefore history, not a live constraint
- ⚠ **COLUMN ORDER IN THE NEW INDEX IS `(channel_id, client_msg_id, author_user_id)`, not the argument order** — the leading pair is what keeps that cross-author read index-served
- **Tests:** `service-writes-idempotency-author.test.ts`, one rule at three layers — the repository QUERY SHAPE (both reads, so a mocked-repository suite cannot be green over an unnarrowed filter), the service behaviour (the attack, two authors → two messages, my own retry idempotent, the race repair, no-key unchanged), and the MIGRATION (the index really carries the author and the pair index is really dropped)
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

## F-260 — the ended-agent window showed nothing, and the 7-day ring written for it had zero callers (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the same review, censusing consumers of `main/agent-history.js` after the ended-agent retention wave
- **THE SHAPE.** `session-engine.js › settle` freezes the narration ring into the durable history BEFORE dropping the registry entry — the ordering is deliberate and is itself pinned. But the read, `session-engine.js › narrationFor`, resolved through `session-registry.js › sessionOn`, which answers `null` for a settled agent **by construction** (that is the ENDED-IS-DEAD rule working correctly). So the ended agent's window opened onto `[]`, and `agent-history.js › historyFor` — written for exactly this read — had **ZERO callers in the tree**
- ⚠ **NEITHER HALF LOOKED BROKEN ON ITS OWN**, which is why it survived a wave: the write is correct, the read is correct, the retention is correct, and the seam between them was never wired. `npx knip` cannot see it — `historyFor` is exported and its module is imported for other members
- **RESOLVED.** `narrationFor` falls back to `agentHistory.historyFor(store.slotKey(a))` when `sessionOn` resolves nothing, returning a COPY of the frozen entries. The key is the one `settle` wrote, all three segments — which is also why an address naming NO agent still gets the live answer alone: `<channel>:<thread>:` matches no frozen record by construction, so the ambiguity fallback can never resolve a dead agent it was not handed
- **Tests:** four cases in `test/agent-ended-is-dead.test.mjs` (the frozen read, the live read still winning, the unnamed address, and the never-throws cases), driving the real `narrationFor` brace-matched out of the shipping engine
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

## F-261 — New Agent on a signed-out machine answered SUCCESS, and the auth-hold refusal was unreachable (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the same review, reading `startSession`'s tail in the order the statements actually execute
- **THE SHAPE.** The SPAWN-IDLE branch (`if (spec.parkedShell) { scheduleIdle(s); return s; }`) sat IN FRONT of `session-auth.js › holdIfNoCredential`. So a machine with no Claude Code sign-in answered `{sessionId, agentId}` — a success — and registered an agent holding a slot against `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS` that could never start a query
- ⚠ **THE REFUSAL SHAPE EXISTED AND WAS SIMPLY UNREACHABLE ON THAT LANE.** `session-launch.js › launch` translates `{authHold:true}` into `{skipped:'auth-hold'}`, and `use-agents-panel.ts › launchRefusalText` has copy for it — on the one lane an operator reaches by CLICKING, neither could fire
- ⚠ **"IT STARTS NO QUERY" IS NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR SKIPPING THE PREFLIGHT.** The whole point of registering is that a later message wakes it; on a signed-out Mac that wake produces a dead session with a peer waiting on it. The credential question is about the MACHINE, not about the first turn
- **RESOLVED.** The windowless rollback branch and the Q6 preflight both run before the spawn-idle return. Nothing else moved — spawn-idle still starts no query, and the abandonment timer is still armed at the spawn
- **Tests:** `test/spawn-idle-auth-hold.test.mjs` evaluates the TAIL of the shipping `startSession` verbatim against fakes (the idiom `main-audit-resume-budget.test.mjs` uses for the same function's preamble), so reordering the statements back fails it; plus the `{skipped:'auth-hold'}` shape on a real spawn-idle spec in `test/session-engine-slot.test.mjs`
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

## F-262 — `deleteTask`'s "no doorbell needed" rested on a replica identity `channel_messages` does not have (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the same review, checking `service-tasks-delete.ts`'s realtime claim against `supabase/migrations`
- **THE FALSE CLAIM, quoted:** the docblock (and INVARIANTS §5, in the same words) said step 1 "fires real DELETEs on `channel_messages`, which IS published and carries `workspace_id` under `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` (`20260807150000`)". That migration set **`USING INDEX`, not FULL**, on eleven tables and named `channel_messages` on its **EXEMPTION** list — "cascade from `channels` / `workspaces` only"
- ⚠ **THE EXEMPTION WAS CORRECT WHEN WRITTEN AND STOPPED BEING TRUE ON 2026-08-21**, when a thread became deletable. Nothing else in that hand-written cascade is published: `channel_tasks` and `channel_sessions` are both deliberately out (§7), and consent rows are UPDATEd to `expired` rather than deleted. So under `REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT` the DELETE's WAL record is the primary key alone, both subscribers' `workspace_id=eq.<id>` filter can never match it, **and every frame is dropped SERVER-SIDE** — the counterparty keeps rendering a thread that no longer exists until a manual refetch, then 404s on click, with no error anywhere
- ⚠ **A STATED REASON IS WHAT MADE THIS FINDABLE.** `ui-sync-replica-identity.test.mjs › NO_DELETE_DOORBELL` maps each exempt table to WHY, and its own instruction is "if the reason has changed, move it to `DELETE_DOORBELL_TABLES` and say so". A bare list would have read as a decision nobody could re-derive
- **RESOLVED.** `supabase/migrations/20260822130000_channel_messages_delete_doorbell.sql` sets `REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX (workspace_id, id)`; the table moves between the two lists in that suite; the docblock and both INVARIANTS bullets (§5 and §7) are corrected rather than softened
- **THE COST, both directions, because the 2026-08-07 file refused this instrument for a reason.** Replica identity is paid on UPDATE and DELETE, never on INSERT — and `channel_messages` has **no UPDATE path in the tree at all** (`repository-messages.ts` is select + one insert RPC + one delete; no migration issues one either), so the marginal cost is +16 bytes of WAL on rows already being deleted. The cost that IS real and is stated in the migration header: a CHANNEL delete now emits one frame per message where it emitted none, bounded by both subscribers' doorbell coalescing
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

## F-263 — `session-summary.js` carried a compatibility re-export with no compatibility to preserve (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the same review, censusing readers of the `session-pill.js` split
- **The shape.** The 2026-08-22 split moved the pill mapping out and left `session-summary.js` re-exporting five names — `PILL_STATES`, `ACTIVITY_PILL`, `pillState`, `queryTornDown`, `listeningState` — "so every existing reader of `summary.pillState` is unchanged". A census found **no production reader of the re-export in either tree**: the only consumers were this suite's harnesses, which already `require` `session-pill.js` directly
- ⚠ **A COMPATIBILITY SHIM WITH NO CALLER IS NOT INERT.** Two names for one function is how a second mapping gets added without anyone deciding to — the exact drift the split was made to prevent (F-142)
- **RESOLVED.** The re-exports are deleted, the `require` narrows to what the file actually calls (`PILL_ENDED`, `pillState`, `listeningState`), and `session-pill.js`'s header no longer claims the shim exists. Pinned by `test/session-summary.test.mjs › BOUNDARY`, which re-RUNS the census over `main/**` rather than restating its result
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22)

## F-264 — a long message body has exactly ONE unclipped read on the MCP surface, and it costs a round-trip per message (2026-08-22)

- Found during: implementing Samuel's ruling that `op="read"` clip long bodies (INVARIANTS §10) — a 128,000-character body was measured in a live read
- **The shape.** `channel-render.ts › clipBody` clips at 2000 chars on any page holding more than one message. The remedy the marker names is `op="read"` with `since=<seq-1>, limit=1`, which is true and works — a one-message page is rendered in full, and that is a stated contract of `formatMessages`. **But it is the ONLY unclipped read, and it returns exactly one message per call.** An agent catching up on a thread carrying three 16k deliverables pays three extra round-trips, each of which is a channel call its operator may have to approve (§10's "what a channel call costs")
- ⚠ **THE OBVIOUS REMEDY IS THE WRONG ONE, and it is worth writing down so nobody reaches for it.** `op="get_thread"` renders **no message bodies at all** — it is title / mode / parties / timestamps (`channel-render.ts › formatThreadDetail`). The ruling this work implemented proposed a marker reading "op get_thread for full"; that would have sent every clipped read to an op that cannot answer, which is the invisible-delivery class of failure the whole addressing lane exists to prevent. **The marker points at `since`/`limit` for that reason, not by preference**
- ⚠ **A THREAD-SCOPED READ IS NOT THE ESCAPE HATCH EITHER.** It was the first candidate — "the caller narrowed deliberately, so give them everything" — and it fails on volume: a thread with forty messages is still a page of forty, and one 128k body in it costs the same context it cost in the channel-wide read. The page SIZE is the thing that decides, which is why the condition is `messages.length > 1`
- Proposed resolution, in preference order: (a) a `full_body=<seq>` argument on `read` that renders ONE named message unclipped inside an ordinary page — no extra call, no cursor confusion, and the clip marker names an argument rather than a second call; (b) raise `BODY_CLIP_CHARS` toward the 16,000 write cap and accept the page arithmetic (100 × 16k is not a page any agent should be handed, so this only helps if `limit` is also lowered); (c) leave it — the extra call is bounded and explicit, and a body over 2000 chars in a transcript scan is rare. **Do not "fix" it by clipping the single-message page for consistency: that breaks the remedy and leaves no unclipped read anywhere**
- Status: open (a product call about the `read` argument surface, not a defect)

## F-265 — `dopl_only` pre-approves the WEB tools that `full` gates, and the safe fix is not the obvious one (2026-08-22)

- Found during: implementing the windowless AXIS A floor (INVARIANTS §11), while measuring whether the *known* inverted-profile bug (`dopl_only` pre-approving `DOPL_READ_TOOLS` that `full` did not) still produced a behavioural difference under the floor. It does not — at `auto` and `bypass`, the only modes a windowless session can now be in, `full` answers `allow` where `dopl_only` answers `preapproved`, and both are ungated. **This second inversion is the one that survives.**
- **The shape.** `main/session-profiles.js › buildSessionToolConfig` puts `WEB_TOOLS` (`WebFetch`, `WebSearch`) in `dopl_only`'s `preApproved` — i.e. the SDK's `allowedTools`, which SHADOWS `canUseTool` entirely. `full` does not, and cannot at `auto`, because both names are in `ESCALATION_TOOLS`: ops that reach the SHELL or the NETWORK and that `auto` deliberately still asks about, since the counterparty's message text steers what the agent proposes. So the RESTRICTED profile reaches the network with no gate and no gate-diag line, while the PERMISSIVE one asks.
- ⚠ **THE RULING'S STATED "SAFE DIRECTION" IS NOT SAFE HERE, which is why this is filed rather than fixed.** For `DOPL_READ_TOOLS` the instruction was "widening `full`'s preApproved is the safe direction — it is already the most permissive profile", and that is true of a read tool. Applying it to `WEB_TOOLS` would pre-approve an ESCALATION tool on the widest profile, shadowing the network past `canUseTool` and emptying `ESCALATION_TOOLS` of meaning for the profile that most needs it.
- **The other direction — narrowing `dopl_only` — is a POSTURE DECISION, not a defect fix.** `dopl_only` is described as "local reads + WEB reads + read-only dopl tools pre-approved", so the web half is deliberate as written; removing it changes what an operator who picked that profile gets. Samuel's call, not this pass's.
- **What is NOT at risk, and was measured:** `SESSION_HARD_DENY`, `buildSecretPathDenyRules` and each profile's `disallowedTools` are unaffected — a hard-denied name is unopenable by any pre-approval, and `read_only` hard-denies `WEB_TOOLS` outright.
- Proposed resolution, in preference order: (a) drop `WEB_TOOLS` from `dopl_only`'s `preApproved` while leaving them in `builtinTools`, so they GATE on that profile exactly as on `full` — one line, and it makes the two profiles order correctly for the first time; (b) leave both as they are and state the inversion in `buildSessionToolConfig`'s docblock as intended, which is where it is recorded today.
- Status: open (a posture call, not a defect — but the two profiles are ordered backwards until it is answered)

## F-266 — the mention masker and the transcript tint are TWO predicates, and they agree only about code (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the v1.17.1 cross-lane verification, checking the "one rule" claim the 2026-08-22 code-span masking landed with (`lib/mentions.ts`, INVARIANTS §5)
- **The shape.** `src/features/channels/lib/mentions.ts › mentionTokensOf` decides what counts as a mention by TEXTUAL masking. `src/features/channels/components/channels-v2/message-markdown.tsx › MentionText` never masks anything — it runs the token regex on whatever `marked` leaves in a `text` / `escape` leaf. The two agreed on backtick spans and ``` / ~~~ fences — the case the rule was about — and diverged everywhere else markdown has structure.
- **MEASURED, not reasoned**, and re-measured at fix time by walking `marked` exactly the way that component walks it and collecting every string that reaches `MentionText`. **TEN divergences, not six:**
  - `**@diana**`, `*@diana*`, `__@diana__`, `_@diana_`, `~~@diana~~` → **TINT, stamp NOBODY.** Root cause is one character class: `TRAILING_PUNCTUATION` contained no `*`, `_` or `~`, so the token stayed `@diana**`.
  - `<b>@diana</b>` → TINTS, stamps nobody (inline `html` tokens render as literal text and the run BETWEEN them is an ordinary leaf).
  - `[@diana](url)` — the link **TEXT** → TINTS, stamps nobody (token was `@diana](url`).
  - `\@diana` → stamps, does NOT tint. **The author escaped it precisely to avoid tagging and got tagged anyway.**
  - `[docs](https://ex.com/@diana)` and `![alt](…)` — link/image **DESTINATIONS** → stamp, do not tint.
  - `[docs]: https://ex.com/@diana` — a link reference definition → stamps, does not tint (`marked` absorbs it and renders nothing).
  - Four-space indented code → stamps, does not tint. **The one that stays open by decision.**
- ⚠ **THE FIRST CLASS IS THE ONE THAT BIT, AND IT WAS TEST-PINNED ON THE WRONG SIDE.** `message-markdown.test.tsx › "tints one inside a bold run, a bullet and a heading"` asserted `**@dianataylor**` renders as a link, so the SPA suite pinned the tint while the server stamped nobody. `**@sam** I am blocked` is exactly how an agent writes the escalation the same wave enabled (`resolveBodyMentions(…, authorIsAgent)`): the tint appeared, the Tags inbox stayed empty, and `main/targeting.js › mentionsMe` never fired because it reads the absent stamp. **Two suites each agreeing with themselves is not the two ends agreeing with each other.**
- ⚠ **ALL OF IT PREDATED THE MASKING WAVE.** `TRAILING_PUNCTUATION` was byte-identical at `66ab053e` and `message-markdown.tsx` was untouched. What the wave introduced was the CLAIM ("Two mechanisms, ONE rule").

**RESOLVED — nine of the ten closed, on the SERVER side only; `message-markdown.tsx` is untouched.**

- **Option (a) taken and widened.** `*`, `_`, `~` joined `TRAILING_PUNCTUATION`, plus a `TRAILING_HTML_TAG` strip for the `<b>…</b>` case. ⚠ **The strip is now a LOOP to a fixed point, not two calls:** `>` is already in the punctuation class, so a single pass in the wrong order turns `@diana</b>` into `@diana</b`, and `**@diana**.` needs two passes whichever order you pick. **F-266's own precondition was verified before `_` was added** — `_` is legal INSIDE a handle, only a TRAILING run is stripped, and `@diana_taylor` resolving whole is pinned.
- **Option (b) declined, deliberately.** Lexing with `marked` on the server would give one predicate, at the cost of putting the markdown engine on the hot write path and making the mention set a function of a parser version. The masks are a sibling module instead.
- **`maskMarkupRegions` (new, `lib/mentions-mask.ts`)** blanks escaped `@`s, link/image destinations and reference definitions, on `maskCodeRegions`'s exact terms. ⚠ **The backslash RUN is counted** — `\\@diana` is an escaped backslash plus a live mention, and blanking `\@` on sight would silently drop a real tag. ⚠ **The destination mask fixes the opposite case for free**, which is why it is a mask and not a token rule: blanking `](url)` leaves exactly `@diana` from `[@diana](url)`, so both halves of a markdown link now match the render.
- ⚠ **ONE ITEM OF THE BRIEF WAS REFUSED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY.** The fix request also asked that autolinks (`<https://…/@diana>`) stop tagging. They must not: `marked` makes the url its own link TEXT, so the transcript **tints them today** — masking them would stamp nothing under a visible highlight, i.e. manufacture a new divergence in the name of closing one. Bare `https://…/@diana` is the same shape. **Both already agreed and were left alone.**
- **THE GUARD IS THE MEASUREMENT, RE-RUNNABLE:** `lib/mentions-tint-parity.test.ts` walks `marked` the way the component walks it, collects every string reaching `MentionText`, and asserts tint === stamp across a 24-row table. It carries a red-proof case and a `TOKEN ARMS` tripwire that reads `message-markdown.tsx`'s source, so a new token arm on that side fails HERE rather than silently making the mirror answer a different question. **It walks the lexer instead of mounting React on purpose** — the question is which strings reach the leaf, and rendering would pin another lane's markup as a side effect.
- **THE ONE SURVIVING GAP IS INDENTED CODE**, excluded from the table BY NAME with its own asserting test, so it stays visible rather than forgotten: `marked` calls a four-space block code and does not tint; the masker does not model it and the server tags. Left alone because deciding whether an indented line is code or a wrapped bullet needs block context, and a chat body indenting prose is common enough that guessing costs real tags. **If it ever closes, that test fails and the row moves into the parity table.**
- **Cap fallout, handled as INVARIANTS §1 requires:** the masks pushed `mentions.ts` to 503 lines, so it was SPLIT (`lib/mentions-mask.ts`, re-exported through `mentions.ts`) rather than having its docblocks trimmed — 346 + 202. The seam is a reason to change: the mask file moves when MARKDOWN's structure does, `mentions.ts` when the HANDLE derivation does.
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22) — nine of ten closed; the indented-code gap is documented, asserted and deliberate.

## F-267 — the operator's own New Agent button resolved its tool profile from the TRAY PROJECTION, so every agent it launched ran `read_only` (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: root-causing a production observation on 2026-08-23 — an agent launched from the Agents tab reporting it had no `dopl_map` / `dopl_members` / `dopl_kb` at all, on a channel whose `agent_tool_profile` is the DB default `full`
- **THE SHAPE, in one hop.** `main/session-ipc-ops.js › sessions:launch` resolved the agent tool profile from `main/channel-listener.js › listWatchedChannels()`. That function is the **TRAY PROJECTION** — its own docblock says so ("for the tray *Channel folders* submenu (id + name only — never cursors/tokens/workspace internals)") — and it returns `{ id, name }` per channel. `main/targeting-window.js › resolveToolProfile` reads `channel.myAgentToolProfile || channel.agentToolProfile`, gets `undefined` off a projection that has neither, and `main/tool-profiles.js › normalizeProfile` **correctly fails closed to `read_only`**. ⚠ **Nothing in the containment layer was wrong. The INPUT was.** Every table, floor, deny list and fail-closed default behaved exactly as designed on an object that was never the right one.
- ⚠ **THE DOCBLOCK ABOVE THE READ ASSERTED THE PROPERTY IT NO LONGER HAD.** It said *"CONTAINMENT: the profile comes from MAIN's own watched-channel record (the server DTO), never the renderer's claim"*. The first half of that sentence was false and the second half was true, which is the worst possible mix: a reviewer checking the renderer-claim question — the interesting one — found it answered and moved on.
- **THE BLAST RADIUS IS REMOVAL, NOT GATING, and that is why it went unnoticed.** `main/session-profiles.js › buildSessionToolConfig('read_only')` puts the whole of `DOPL_SAFE_TOOLS` into `disallowedTools` and bounds `builtinTools` to `READ_BUILTINS`. A hard-denied name never reaches `grantDecision`, so **no Axis-A floor can reopen it**: `dopl_map`, `dopl_members`, `dopl_kb`, `dopl_search`, `dopl_skill`, `dopl_ontology`, `dopl_chats`, `current_workspace` and `list_workspaces` were **absent from the model's context**, leaving `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob`/`LS`/`TodoWrite` plus the op-scoped `mcp__dopl__dopl_channel`. An agent that cannot see a tool does not report being denied it — it reports not having it, or quietly works around it.
- ⚠ **THE TWO LAUNCH LANES DISAGREED ABOUT THE SAME CHANNEL, WHICH IS THE PART THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN CHECKABLE.** `main/trigger.js › handleTrigger` resolves from the full `entry.channel` DTO and has been right the whole time, so a peer-triggered responder ran `full` on the very channel where the operator's own click ran `read_only`. **Neither lane had a test asserting which PROFILE it resolves.** `test/channel-launch-posture.test.mjs` — the file whose name reads as if it covered this — covers the DURABLE POSTURE's two PERMISSION axes (supervision), and says nothing about containment; the census in `test/session-preset-census.test.mjs` counts CONSUMERS of the posture record, not inputs to `normalizeProfile`. **A fail-closed default is invisible to every test that only asserts "restrictive is fine".**

**RESOLVED — the smallest correct shape: a second accessor, not a wider projection.**

- **`main/channel-listener.js › watchedChannel(channelId)` (new, exported)** returns the stored `entry.channel` DTO off the `loops` map, or `null` for a channel main is not watching. It sits beside `listWatchedChannels`, which is **UNCHANGED in shape** and keeps returning `{ id, name }` for the tray — `main/index.js › getChannels` is still on it, and its docblock now says the projection must stay one. **Two readers because there are two questions**, not one reader widened to serve both: handing a menu builder the server DTO is how the next projection stops being one.
- **`sessions:launch` now reads `targeting.resolveToolProfile(listener.watchedChannel(p.channelId))`** — the same object `trigger.js` hands the same resolver, so **the two lanes cannot disagree by construction.** The containment property is preserved and the docblock is now TRUE: main's own record, never the renderer's claim. Fail-closed is unchanged and covers both holes — an unwatched channel resolves `null`, a watched DTO with no profile field resolves `undefined`, and `normalizeProfile` floors both at `read_only`.
- **NOT TOUCHED, deliberately** (each verified correct while reading): `floorWindowlessTool`, `SESSION_HARD_DENY`, `AUTO_TOOLS`/`BYPASS_TOOLS`, `buildSessionToolConfig`'s per-profile tables, and `normalizeProfile`'s fail-closed default. Only the input moved.
- **`test/launch-tool-profile.test.mjs` (new) pins the axis that was unpinned**, driving the SHIPPED `session-ipc-ops.js` through its real sender binding with the REAL resolver and the REAL profile table (a permissive stub would accept exactly the input that caused this), and the registry accessors SLICED out of the shipped listener rather than re-implemented. Cases: a watched `full` channel resolves `full` (red at v1.17.1); a watched `read_only` channel resolves `read_only` for the right reason; unwatched and field-less both fail closed; **the two lanes agree over every entry**; the projection fed back in floors even the `full` channel; `sessions:launch` names no `listWatchedChannels`; and `read_only` really REMOVES `DOPL_SAFE_TOOLS` rather than gating them. ⚠ **Verified red-proof against the pre-fix read**: restoring the projection lookup fails 4 of the 11, the headline case among them.
- ⚠ **BOTH FILES WERE AT 499 OF THE 500-LINE CAP**, so the fix had to be line-NEUTRAL — the state `session-ipc-ops.js`'s own header warns about ("a file at the cap does not just stop growing; it stops being correctable"). Paid for in the same neighbourhood rather than by trimming the new comment to nothing: `listWatchedChannels`'s body was compacted to the equivalent chain, and three narrow-wrapped comment blocks in `channel-listener.js` were reflowed to the file's own width with no content dropped. Both files are 499 again. **This is the second entry in three days whose real cost was the cap, and F-226's headline still stands.**
- **DOC CORRECTIONS IN THE SAME CHANGE** (CLAUDE.md precedence — a false INVARIANTS claim is a defect): §11's 2026-08-22 Axis-A floor bullet claimed flooring at `auto` makes `DOPL_READ_TOOLS` reachable without a gate, **which was false on this lane as shipped** — they were not in the context to be reached. It now states the precondition (the profile must resolve to `full`; `dopl_only` pre-approves them instead; `read_only` hard-denies them) and that the floor widens only as far as the profile already reaches. §11 gained a bullet stating the AGREEMENT rule and naming both lanes' inputs. ⚠ **The identical overstatement also sits in `main/session-profiles.js › floorWindowlessTool`'s docblock and was LEFT ALONE** — a concurrent read-only investigation is in that file and a comment edit there is a collision for no behavioural gain. **It is the next reader's to correct, and it is named here so it is not re-derived from scratch.**
- **STALE ANCHORS FIXED (six).** `channel-prefs.js` (×2), `trigger.js`, `session-launch.js`, `test/channel-launch-posture.test.mjs` and `test/preload-parity.test.mjs` all cited `channel-dir-ipc.js › sessions:launch`; the handler has lived in `session-ipc-ops.js` since the 2026-08-20 split. `test/session-preset-start.test.mjs`'s prose said the same and is corrected (its own `⚠ REPOINTED` note was already right — the file was arguing with itself). ⚠ **INVARIANTS §11 was NOT among them**: it already names `session-ipc-ops.js` with the split as a parenthetical, and it is correct as written. **`check-doc-refs` cannot see any of these** — it resolves `path › symbol` anchors inside `docs/` and scans source trees for `F-NNN` ids only, so a symbol anchor in a source comment is unchecked. **That blind spot is what let six anchors survive a two-day-old file split, and it is stated here rather than filed because closing it is a checker change, not a code one.**
- Status: **RESOLVED** (2026-08-22). ⚠ **A live containment defect, not debt** — shipped in v1.17.1 and every release back to the 2026-08-20 split.

## F-268 — the SDK session loaded NINE claude.ai account connectors from a lane no option covers, and `settingSources: []` is what removed the off switch (2026-08-22) — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-22

- Found during: the read-only investigation that ran alongside F-267's fix, asking whether claude.ai connector tools reach a windowless session despite `settingSources: []`. Samuel approved R1 + R3a; his veto window passed.
- **THE MECHANISM, verified against the bundled binary.** The CLI has a **THIRD MCP LANE** beside the two `session-query.js › buildSdkOptions` controls. When the session's OAuth credential carries the `user:mcp_servers` scope, it fetches `GET /v1/mcp_servers` with that Bearer and connects **every claude.ai ACCOUNT CONNECTOR** as `mcp__claude_ai_<Name>__*`. `mcpServers` does not cover it (that field adds servers, it does not bound the set) and neither does `settingSources`.
- ⚠ **THE IRONY IS THE FINDING.** The CLI ships an off switch — the `disableClaudeAiConnectors` **setting** — and `settingSources: []`, our own isolation, is exactly what makes it unreadable. **Tightening the sandbox deleted the control.** A hardening measure removed the mechanism that would have prevented the leak it was hardening against.
- ⚠ **INVARIANTS §11's SDK-LANE COLUMN SAID "DO NOT LOAD" WHILE NINE SERVERS LOADED**, and the prose called the lane "narrowed by construction". Both claims are enumerations of the options WE SET, presented as a description of the child's whole world. **A construction argument is only as wide as the constructor.** Corrected in the same change, with the measurement.

**MEASURED 2026-08-22** — bundled binary `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude`, **claude 2.1.220 / claude-agent-sdk 0.3.220**. Command: `[ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=<v>] "$BIN" --print --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 1 "Reply with the single word OK and nothing else."`, reading the `system`/`init` message's `mcp_servers`:

| `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` | total servers | claude.ai connectors | `dopl` entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| (unset) | 12 | **9** | present |
| `''` | 12 | **9** | present |
| `'0'` | 3 | **0** | present |
| `'false'` | 3 | **0** | present |

The nine were Slack, Figma, Dopl, Attio, Notion, Granola, Google Drive, Google Calendar and Gmail.

**RESOLVED — R1 (suppress at the process boundary) + R3a (framing belt). R3b deferred.**

- **R1: `runtime/claude/loader.js › buildScrubbedEnv` sets `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS='0'`,** written **last and unconditionally** so an inherited `=1` in the parent env cannot re-admit the lane (the name does not match `PERMISSION_ENV_RE`, so it would otherwise copy straight through the scrub loop). Exported as `CLAUDEAI_MCP_ENV` / `CLAUDEAI_MCP_OFF` so the value has one definition.
- ⚠ **POLARITY WAS INFERRED FROM MINIFIED CODE AND THEN VERIFIED TWICE, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON IT IS TRUSTED.** Statically: the eligibility chain is `if (su(process.env.ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS) || <setting>) return {}`, and `su` is `e === undefined ? false : typeof e === 'boolean' ? !e : ['0','false','no','off'].includes(String(e).toLowerCase().trim())` — i.e. **"explicitly set FALSY"**, so a var named `ENABLE_` *disables*. Empirically: the table above. ⚠ **`''` IS A SILENT NO-OP** — `su('')` is false, so *clearing* this var re-admits nine servers and nothing errors. That trap is a test case, not a comment.
- **R3a: `prompt-framing-text.js › LANE_EXCLUSIVITY`**, spread into `prompt-framing.js › firstActions` so it rides **both sides**: `mcp__dopl__dopl_channel` is the only path off this machine, and no other `mcp__` server (Slack, Gmail, Drive, anything that is not `mcp__dopl__`) is this session's lane. ⚠ **It went in the TEXT module, not the assembly module, because that is the seam that file's own header declares** — fixed text with nothing interpolated — and because `prompt-framing.js` was at 499 of the cap. Two rules it had to clear: no em dash (`prompt-framing.test.mjs` scans every line naming `dopl_channel`) and no `task=`.
- ⚠ **NEITHER HALF IS THE CONTAINMENT, and the entry says so where it cannot be skimmed past.** Execution was never reachable: connector tools are unclassified, `AUTO_TOOLS`/`BYPASS_TOOLS` are positive allow-lists, so `grantDecision` gates them and a windowless session denies — all 12 profile × mode cells pinned by `session-tool-name-prefix.test.mjs`. **What this removes is the OFFERED SURFACE:** an inventory of the operator's connected accounts sitting in a prompt that can be auto-sent, and its per-turn token cost across every live session.
- **`--strict-mcp-config` REJECTED, and the rejection is pinned.** It would suppress the lane, and it hard-errors on machines carrying an enterprise `managed-mcp.json` — trading a leak for a launch failure on the fleet least able to debug it. `test/claudeai-connector-lane.test.mjs` asserts it has not crept into either file.
- **R3b (deny-on-unclassified) DEFERRED, deliberately.** The gate already holds, and inverting a positive allow-list is a change to make on its own terms, not as a side effect of this one. `AUTO_TOOLS` / `BYPASS_TOOLS` / `grantDecision` untouched.
- **`test/claudeai-connector-lane.test.mjs` (new, 13 cases).** ⚠ **Its header states outright that no case in it can prove the lane is off** — the only authority is the child's own init message, so the empirical table above is recorded IN the test header, dated, with the reproducing command. What the cases pin is the join, per §11's rule that an env assertion is necessary and not sufficient: the var is set, minted when absent, **overrides any inherited value**, is inside the binary's falsy set while `''` is not; the scrub's existing jobs (permission knobs dropped, auth preserved) survive; `options.env` is built from `buildScrubbedEnv` at the one assembly point and nothing rewrites it; `withStoredCredential` adds a key rather than replacing the object on all four credential shapes; `settingSources: []` and the env var are pinned **together, as the join that explains why the var exists**; `strictMcpConfig` is absent; and the framing belt reaches a built turn on both sides. ⚠ **Red-proof verified two ways**: deleting the assignment reds 5 cases, and changing the value to `''` — the plausible "cleanup" edit — reds the same 5.
